brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn about the long-term effects on health and well-being of treatment for overweight in childhood or adolescence using the Children's Obesity Clinic Treatment protocol (the Holbæk Model) (HM).

The study has two parts:

* An active follow-up study, where participants are invited to take part in new measurements and questionnaires
* A register-based study, which uses existing data on diagnoses, medication use, and school well-being The submitted protocol primarily focuses on the active follow-up study. The register-based study covers diagnoses, medication use, and school-related well-being and is described in the section "Detailed description".

In the active follow-up study, researchers will examine:

* Body measurements such as height, weight, and waist circumference
* Body composition
* Psychosocial well-being and mental health
* Eating behaviors in young adults Participants will be followed for up to 20 years after treatment initiation. Where possible, results will be compared with a group of people of the same age from the same area who did not receive this treatment. This will help show whether their development differs from that of the general population.

The aim is to use the findings to improve future follow-up care and support for people who were treated for overweight as children.

The study includes two groups:

1. A treatment group of individuals treated at the Holbæk Pediatric Department between 2008 and 2025
2. A comparison group from the general population, recruited between 2010 and 2016

The study will take place in two phases:

* A pilot phase (about 1.5 years) to test procedures and recruitment
* A main phase (about 3 years)

Participants are invited to one follow-up visit. During this visit:

* Body measurements will be taken
* Body composition will be assessed
* Participants will complete questionnaires The study team will ensure that all participants are treated respectfully and without stigma. Flexible options, including home visits, are offered to make participation easier.
interventions: The AFTER study - Assessing Future Trajectories of hEalth- and well-being among childhood obesity treatment Recipients
title: Long-term Follow-up After Childhood Obesity

brief_summary: The original, "Cut Your Pressure Too: The LA Barbershop Blood Pressure Study (LABBPS)" (NCT02321618) was a highly successful cluster-randomized trial of a community centered blood pressure (BP) reduction program focused on Non-Hispanic (NH) black men who experience the highest rates of hypertension (HTN) and its complications. Patrons of 52 barbershops in Los Angeles County were randomly assigned to either an intervention arm in which barbers encouraged meetings with trained clinical pharmacists who provided HTN treatment in the barbershops or a control arm in which barbers provided educational pamphlets on HTN and encouraged physician appointments. After 6 months, the intervention group had a statistically significant reduction in systolic BP (SBP) of 21.6 mmHg compared to the control group. Results were durable at 1 year. Thereafter, a pilot study (NCT03726710) aimed at improving the efficiency of the barbershop model of HTN care by substituting in-person visits with video visits once BP was at goal was undertaken in 10 hypertensive barbershop patrons. The intervention effect was unchanged. The current study represents Aim 3 of an NIH funded renewal application entitled, "Barber and Pharmacist Coordination to Improve Blood Pressure Management in Black Men." It will build upon the foundational work of the original study and telemedicine pilot by evaluating the efficacy of a fully remote hypertension management program.
title: Barber and Pharmacist Coordination to Improve Blood Pressure Management

brief_summary:
This pilot study will evaluate whether microsurgical modification of cervical lymphatic drainage may influence blood biomarkers and clinical outcomes in people with mild Alzheimer's disease.

Thirty participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either a surgical intervention group or a control group. Participants in the intervention group will undergo supermicrosurgical lymphaticovenous anastomosis (LVA) and/or lymph node-to-vein anastomosis (LNVA) in the neck to create an alternative pathway for lymphatic drainage. The procedure may be performed manually or with robotic microsurgical assistance. Participants in the control group will receive clinical observation without surgery during the first 12 months.

The primary objective is to assess the change in plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) from baseline to 12 months. The study will also assess changes in cognitive and functional measures, including CDR-Sum, ADCS-ADL, MoCA, and MMSE, as well as the feasibility and safety of the surgical procedure.

Participants will be assessed at baseline and at 3, 6, and 12 months. After completion of the 12-month observation period, participants in the control group may be offered the surgical procedure if they wish to undergo it.
primary_outcomes: Change in Plasma Phosphorylated Tau 217 (p-tau217) Concentration From Baseline to Month 12
title: Cervical Lymphatic Microsurgery in Alzheimer's Disease

brief_summary:
Recurrent weight gain affects 15% to 40% of patients after metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS). SG is the most performed operation worldwide, and long-term regain after SG is well documented. A 2026 international Delphi consensus has now standardized the definition. This trial uses that definition. So does our companion trial, RESURGE.

We have two real treatments. Both work. Neither is enough. Conversion of SG to RYGB gives around 20% additional total weight loss at 12 months across all indications, and less when the indication is poor weight response rather than reflux. Drug therapy also works after MBS. Liraglutide beat placebo by about 8 percentage points in the BARI-OPTIMISE randomized trial. Semaglutide gives around 11% total weight loss and tirzepatide around 14% in pooled retrospective data, including specifically after SG. Most patients do not return to their nadir weight with either option alone.

The field is already comparing the two strategies, but only retrospectively. Two 2025 multicenter cohorts compared conversion against GLP-1 therapy after SG. These studies cannot control diet, exercise, supplementation, co-medication, or adherence. They cannot settle the question.

The societies agree on the pathway but admit the evidence is weak. The 2024 IFSO position statement and the 2026 ASMBS statement say the same thing: work up the anatomy first; operate when there is a structural problem; consider medical therapy when there is not; and consider combining drug therapy with revision. The 2024 IFSO international consensus goes further: with 92% agreement, it states that medications should generally be considered before revisional surgery for recurrent weight gain. Every one of those recommendations rests on consensus and retrospective data. None rests on a randomized trial. This protocol is that trial.
lead_sponsor: General Committee of Teaching Hospitals and Institutes, Egypt
title: Semaglutide Given Before and After Conversion of Sleeve Gastrectomy to Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass for Recurrent Weight Gain

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether brief psychoanalytic therapy and cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) reduce depressive symptoms in adults aged 18 to 65 who have been diagnosed with major depressive disorder. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does brief psychoanalytic therapy reduce depression severity more than a waitlist control condition after 18 weeks?
* Does CBT reduce depression severity more than a waitlist control condition after 18 weeks?

Researchers will also compare brief psychoanalytic therapy with CBT to explore whether one works better than the other, and will examine whether changes in defense mechanisms and automatic negative thoughts explain improvement in each therapy.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to brief psychoanalytic therapy, CBT, or a waitlist control group (30 participants per group)
* In the therapy groups, attend 18 weekly individual therapy sessions of 50 minutes each
* In the waitlist group, continue their usual psychiatric care without psychotherapy for 18 weeks, and then be offered one of the therapies
* Complete clinical interviews and questionnaires about depression, anxiety, quality of life, thought patterns and coping styles before treatment, at week 9 and at week 18
* In the therapy groups, complete follow-up assessments 6 and 12 months after treatment ends
title: Brief Psychoanalytic Therapy Versus Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Major Depressive Disorder

brief_summary: Stroke is a leading cause of neurological disability and upper limb impairment. While conventional rehabilitation options exist, brain-computer interface (BCI)-based neurorehabilitation has emerged as a promising approach that records and decodes neural signals to drive rehabilitation devices or functional electrical stimulation. By re-coupling cortical motor intent to limb movement, BCI systems restore closed-loop neurofeedback and facilitate neuroplasticity through residual neural pathways. Motor intent is detected non-invasively via scalp electroencephalography (EEG), using characteristic changes in mu and beta rhythm activity known as event-related desynchronisation (ERD). This study aims to investigate how these electrophysiological signals change over time following stroke and their implications for BCI-based rehabilitation.
interventions: BCI-Based Neurorehabilitation with Functional Electrical Stimulation (recoveriX)
title: Brain-computer Interface (BCI)-Guided Upper Limb Neurorehabilitation for Acute Stroke With the recoveriX System

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether the size of the opening made during laser-assisted cataract surgery affects where the artificial lens sits in the eye and the glasses prescription after surgery.

This study includes adults aged 40 years and older who are scheduled to have cataract surgery in both eyes. Cataract surgery removes the cloudy natural lens of the eye and replaces it with a clear artificial lens, called an intraocular lens.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Does the size of the capsulotomy (the circular opening made during surgery) affect the final position of the lens implant?
* Does capsulotomy size affect vision or glasses prescription after surgery?

Each participant will receive two different capsulotomy sizes, one in each eye. The size (big or small) used in each eye is chosen by chance. Both sizes are safe and commonly used during cataract surgery. All surgeries use a laser system that allows the opening to be made very precisely.

Participants will:

* Attend one study visit before surgery for eye exams and imaging
* Undergo standard cataract surgery in both eyes using laser assistance
* Attend one final study visit about 12 weeks after the second surgery for repeat eye exams and imaging

Participants will receive the same type of lens implant and standard follow-up care whether or not they join the study. There is no direct benefit from taking part. The information learned may help doctors improve planning and accuracy for future cataract surgeries.
interventions: Femtosecond Laser Capsulotomy - Small Size (4.6 mm)
Femtosecond Laser Capsulotomy - Large Size (5.6 mm)
title: The Effect of Capsulotomy Size on Effective Lens Position in Robotic Laser Cataract Surgery

brief_summary:
The leadless pacemaker is a novel pacing technology that has emerged in recent years. Compared with conventional lead pacemakers, its design avoids many complications associated with leads and pacemaker pockets, including lead fracture, pocket infection, and venous access stenosis. Because of its small size and the absence of a pacemaker pocket or pacing lead, the leadless pacemaker is particularly suitable for patients with contraindications to conventional pacemaker implantation, including patients undergoing hemodialysis, patients with recurrent pocket infection, and patients without suitable vascular access.

Currently, leadless pacemaker implantation is performed primarily under fluoroscopic guidance. Fluoroscopy provides real-time intraoperative anatomical localization information but places high demands on the operator's technical skills and the precise intraoperative positioning of the pacemaker. However, procedures performed under fluoroscopic guidance require dedicated procedure rooms and radiation-generating equipment. Such large-scale equipment is expensive, and it requires special protective measures that make the surrounding walls, doors and windows meet the protection standards, so as not to cause harm to the surrounding environment and personnel. When procedures are performed under fluoroscopic guidance in dedicated catheterization laboratories, both operators and patients are exposed to potential health risks, and fluoroscopy-guided procedures are contraindicated in some pregnant women. In addition, X-ray imaging remains two-dimensional, and visualization may be inadequate in some patients because of individual anatomical variation, potentially increasing procedural difficulty. Therefore, exploring a radiation-free, real-time, and accurate guidance method has become a key approach to improving the success rate and safety of leadless pacemaker implantation.
lead_sponsor: China National Center for Cardiovascular Diseases
primary_outcomes: Successful implantation of the Micra leadless pacemaker
title: Ultrasound Guided Leadless Pacemaker Implantation

brief_summary: This study aims to determine the prevalence of shrimp sensitization and clinical shrimp allergy among patients aged ≥7 years with confirmed allergy to edible insects, including silkworm, bamboo worm, and palm weevil. Participants undergo skin prick testing, specific IgE testing, ALEX2, immunoblot analysis, and risk-based oral food challenges to assess clinical cross-reactivity between edible insects and white shrimp and to help avoid unnecessary shrimp restriction.
primary_outcomes: To determine the prevalence of shrimp sensitization and clinical shrimp allergy among patients with a history of edible insect allergy.
title: Shrimp Sensitization and Allergy Among Patients With Edible Insect Allergy

brief_summary:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction is commonly associated with moderate to severe postoperative pain, particularly during the early postoperative period and rehabilitation. Effective postoperative analgesia is important to facilitate early mobilization, improve patient comfort, and reduce opioid consumption and opioid-related adverse effects.

Adductor canal block (ACB) is commonly used as part of multimodal analgesia for knee surgery because it provides analgesia while largely preserving quadriceps motor function. However, ACB primarily targets the anteromedial aspect of the knee and may provide limited analgesia for pain arising from the posterior and posterolateral knee.

The biceps femoris short head (BiFeS) block is a motor-sparing fascial plane block targeting sensory contributions to the posterolateral knee region. Combining BiFeS block with ACB may therefore provide more comprehensive analgesia than ACB alone.

This randomized study aims to compare the postoperative analgesic efficacy of adductor canal block alone with adductor canal block combined with BiFeS block in patients undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction surgery.
interventions: Adductor Canal Block + BiFeS Block Group
title: Comparison of Analgesic Effects of ACB Versus ACB Combined With BiFeS Block in ACL Reconstruction Surgery

brief_summary:
We have developed a digital assistant based on GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer) technology, trained specifically to provide empathetic, medically accurate, and guideline-based responses in Hebrew, tailored to the clinical protocols used in our clinic.

The goal of this interventional study is to learn about the feasibility, usability, and acceptability of a GPT-based digital assistant for patients undergoing medication abortion or treatment for missed abortion.

The study aims to assess use of the digital assistant, patient-reported usability, usefulness and satisfaction, perceived support, comprehension of treatment instructions, and decisions about contacting medical staff.

Participants already receiving standard care for medication abortion or missed abortion at the clinic will be offered access to the digital assistant immediately after enrollment. They may use the assistant freely at home throughout their treatment process and will complete baseline and follow-up surveys about their experience, emotional state, and any additional contacts with the clinic.
primary_outcomes: Feasibility and usage rates of the digital assistant
Patient satisfaction, usability, and perceived usefulness
Patient-reported decision not to contact medical staff after using the assistant
Perceived support and availability of answers
title: GPT-Based Digital Assistant Support During Treatment for Induced Abortion or Missed Abortion

brief_summary: This multicenter retrospective study aims to develop, validate, and clinically apply an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered electrocardiography (ECG) algorithm for the diagnosis and prognostic prediction of cardiovascular diseases, including coronary artery disease and heart failure. By utilizing encrypted raw 12-lead ECG text data and deep neural network models, the study evaluates the effectiveness of AI-enhanced ECG in detecting cardiac abnormalities and predicting clinical outcomes.
interventions: AI-based ECG Diagnostic and Localization Algorithm
title: AI-Based Differential Diagnosis and Localization of Tachycardia Using ECG: Multicenter Registry (EP-AI ASSIST)

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled trial is to determine whether a Storyline-based gamified blended learning (SGBL) intervention improves electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation competence and self-reported clinical decision-making among undergraduate nursing students.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does the SGBL intervention improve students' ECG interpretation competence compared with conventional face-to-face education? Does the SGBL intervention improve students' self-reported clinical decision-making compared with conventional face-to-face education? Researchers will compare the SGBL intervention with conventional face-to-face, lecture-based education covering the same educational content.

Participants will:

Attend six weekly face-to-face educational sessions, each lasting 90 minutes. Receive either the SGBL intervention or conventional face-to-face instruction. Complete assessments of ECG interpretation competence and self-reported clinical decision-making before the intervention and two weeks after completion of the educational program.
title: Storyline-Based Gamified Blended Learning for ECG Interpretation in Nursing Students

brief_summary: This study will be conducted as a randomized controlled crossover study to evaluate the effects of different positions during skin-to-skin contact on physiological parameters, comfort, and feeding tolerance in preterm infants receiving orogastric feeding. Preterm infants who meet the eligibility criteria will be included in the study. Each infant will receive orogastric feeding while being held in different positions during skin-to-skin contact, according to the assigned sequence. Physiological parameters, including heart rate, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, and body temperature, will be assessed during the feeding sessions. Infants' comfort levels will be evaluated using the Neonatal Comfort Behavior Scale, and feeding tolerance will be assessed based on clinical signs and abdominal measurements. The findings will be compared across the different positioning conditions to determine their effects on physiological stability, comfort, and feeding tolerance in preterm infants.
interventions: Skin-to-Skin Contact in a Semi-Elevated Right Lateral Position
Skin-to-Skin Contact in an Upright Position
title: Effects of Different Positions During Skin-to-Skin Contact in Preterm Infants Receiving Orogastric Feeding

brief_summary:
The primary objective of this study is to evaluate changes in participant-reported gastrointestinal function over a 16-week intervention period and a 4-week non-supplementation period (20 weeks total) following daily consumption of two different doses of colostrum in comparison to a placebo.

Secondary objectives include evaluation of digestive comfort, immune resilience, energy levels, sleep quality, hsCRP, metabolic panel, microbiome status and function, and hair and skin health.

Exploratory objectives include the collection of physical activity status and pulse rate variability at specified timepoints to provide supportive contextual information alongside participant-reported outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Change in Gastrointestinal Function Assessed by the PROMIS Gastrointestinal Combined Short Form
title: Colostrum and Gut Health

brief_summary: This study was conducted to investigate the effects of incorporating synchronized voluntary muscle activation and active motor engagement during neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) into a lumbar stabilization exercise program in individuals with chronic non-specific low back pain. Thirty-six individuals with chronic non-specific low back pain were randomly assigned to two groups. Both groups participated in an 8-week lumbar stabilization exercise program combined with NMES, administered twice weekly. The experimental group performed synchronized voluntary muscle activation and active motor engagement during NMES, whereas the control group received NMES without voluntary muscle activation. Pain intensity, disability, trunk endurance, lumbopelvic motor control, stabilization parameters, depression, fear-avoidance beliefs, and trunk range of motion were assessed to evaluate the effects of the intervention.
title: Effects of Mental Participation During Lumbar Stabilization and Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation in Chronic Non-Specific Low Back Pain

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the pharmacokinetics (PK), safety, and tolerability of sulthiame in participants with mild and moderate renal impairment compared to those in healthy participants with normal renal function.

brief_summary: This observational study aims to compare the predictive performance of the Modified El-Ganzouri Risk Index (MEGRI) incorporating anthropometric ratios with the original El-Ganzouri Risk Index (EGRI) for predicting difficult intubation in obese adult patients undergoing elective general anesthesia.
primary_outcomes: Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) of the Modified El-Ganzouri Risk Index for Predicting Difficult Intubation

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if the "Insul-In This Together" family program works to improve outcomes for adolescents living with type 1 diabetes. It will also learn about how the program influences diabetes-related factors, including parenting. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does this program improve glycemic (blood glucose) outcomes? Does this program improve adolescent quality of life related to diabetes? Researchers will offer the program to all participating families, with one group receiving the program right after enrollment and another group receiving the program 6 months later.

Adolescent and parent participants will:

Attend 8 weekly 30-minute videoconference sessions with an interventionist Complete online surveys, share diabetes device data, and conduct at-home A1c tests 3-5 times over a 12-month period
title: Insul-In This Together: Leveraging Family Support and Diabetes Technology for Adolescents Living With Type 1 Diabetes

brief_summary: Alcohol use and sexual violence are significant public health issues affecting military personnel. This study includes a pilot randomized control trial of Positive Change© for Sailors, an integrated alcohol and sexual assault prevention program tailored to U.S. Navy personnel. Active duty Sailors aged 18-24 will be randomized to receive Positive Change© for Sailors or an assessment-only control condition. Analyses will be conducted to assess feasibility and examine preliminary differences in behavior, perceived norms, and related attitudes immediately following the program and at a three month follow-up assessment.
title: Positive Change for Sailors

brief_summary:
Many families of young children with autism in India wait a long time for a diagnosis and specialist therapy, and receive little structured guidance on how to help their child at home. PRIME-ASD is a 12-week programme in which a trained therapist coaches parents or other main caregivers to use simple, play-based activities within everyday household and cultural routines to support their child's social interaction, communication, emotions, behaviour, sensory responses and thinking skills.

This study will test whether PRIME-ASD, added to usual care, reduces autism symptoms more than usual care alone. A total of 188 children aged 2-9 years with autism attending AIIMS Bhubaneswar, Odisha, India, will be randomly assigned in equal numbers to receive PRIME-ASD plus usual care or usual care alone. Autism symptoms will be measured with the Indian Scale for Assessment of Autism (ISAA) by assessors who do not know which group the child is in. The main comparison is at 12 weeks; the study will also look at behaviour, social maturity, whether any benefit lasts to 24 weeks, whether families can take part and find the programme acceptable, and safety. Some caregivers will be interviewed about their experience of delivering the programme at home.
interventions: Behavioral: PRIME-ASD (Parent-led Intervention Module for Early Autism Spectrum Disorder)
Behavioral: PRIME-ASD; Other: Treatment as usual
lead_sponsor: All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Bhubaneswar
primary_outcomes: Change in autism symptom severity (ISAA total score) at 12 weeks
title: Development and Evaluation of a Parent-led Intervention Module for Early Autism Spectrum Disorder (PRIME-ASD) in Odisha, India: Protocol for a Multiphase Mixed-methods Study Including an Open-label Randomised Controlled Trial

brief_summary: This study investigates the effects of a multidimensional, 13-component sleep hygiene optimization intervention on cognitive performance (executive functions, cognitive flexibility, and psychomotor speed) and objective sleep parameters in elite female sitting volleyball athletes. The study aims to optimize the on-court decision-making mechanisms of Paralympic athletes by improving sleep quality through structured environmental and behavioral factors.
primary_outcomes: Objective Cognitive Performance Analysis using the Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT) and Stroop Test (TBAG Form)
title: Cognitive Functions in Women's National Sitting Volleyball Players

brief_summary: This clinical study is designed to evaluate the effects of different irrigation agitation techniques and root canal sealers on postoperative pain and oral health-related quality of life in patients with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis. Postoperative pain following root canal treatment may affect patient comfort and satisfaction. The choice of irrigation agitation technique and root canal sealer may influence these outcomes. Irrigation agitation techniques are used to improve cleaning of the root canal system. XP-Endo Finisher, EDDY, and passive ultrasonic activation use different mechanisms to enhance this process. Root canal sealers, including the epoxy resin-based AH Plus and the calcium silicate-based NeoSealer Flo, also differ in their composition and biological properties. Clinical evidence regarding the combined effects of these techniques and sealers on patient-reported outcomes remains limited. In this randomized clinical trial, 324 patients aged 18-65 years requiring root canal treatment for a single-rooted, single-canal permanent tooth with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis will be allocated to six groups. Each group will receive one of three irrigation agitation techniques-XP-Endo Finisher, EDDY, or passive ultrasonic activation-in combination with either AH Plus or NeoSealer Flo. Root canal treatment will be completed in a single visit. Postoperative pain intensity will be assessed using a visual analog scale at 6, 12, 24, 48, and 72 hours and 7 days after treatment. Oral health-related quality of life will be assessed using the Oral Health Impact Profile-14 questionnaire before treatment and 7 days afterward. Analgesic use during the follow-up period will also be recorded. The primary objective is to compare postoperative pain among the six treatment groups. Secondary objectives include evaluating changes in oral health-related quality of life and analgesic consumption. The study will also investigate whether irrigation agitation techniques and root canal sealers have interacting effects on postoperative pain. The findings may help clinicians select irrigation agitation techniques and root canal sealers that support patient comfort and improve the patient experience following root canal treatment.
title: Effects of Different Root Canal Filling Materials and Irrigation Agitation Techniques on Postoperative Pain in Teeth With Irreversible Pulpitis: A Randomized Clinical Trial

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effects of exercise combined with kinesiology taping on local hemodynamic parameters in healthy university students. Doppler ultrasound will be used to assess local blood flow and hemodynamic responses associated with the intervention. Participants will perform the exercise protocol with kinesiology taping, and hemodynamic parameters will be assessed to determine whether the combined intervention produces changes in local circulation. The study is designed to provide a better understanding of the acute circulatory responses to exercise combined with kinesiology taping.
primary_outcomes: Blood Flow Volume of the Lower-Limb Arteries
title: Doppler Ultrasound Evaluation of the Effects of Exercise Combined With Kinesiology Taping on Local Hemodynamic Parameters

brief_summary:
This is a 16-week randomized controlled trial (RCT) with outcome assessor blinding. The objective is to investigate the effects of resistance training (RT) combined with whole-body neuromuscular electrical stimulation (WB-NMES) and a high-protein diet on body composition, anthropometry, and quality of life.

Sample and Group Allocation

The sample will comprise 36 older adults (≥ 60 years), physically inactive, and with overweight or obesity (BMI ≥ 25 kg/m²). They will be randomized (stratified by sex) into four groups of 9 participants:

RT + NOR: Resistance training + normal-protein diet.

RT + PRO: Resistance training + high-protein diet.

WB-NMES + RT + NOR: Resistance training with electrical stimulation + normal-protein diet.

WB-NMES + RT + PRO: Resistance training with electrical stimulation + high-protein diet.

Intervention Protocol

Exercise (2x/week, 25 min/session): Seven exercises (2 sets of 1 min execution with 45s of rest). Progressive intensity controlled by the OMNI-RPE Scale.

Electrical Stimulation (WB-NMES Groups): Simultaneous use of an electrode suit (85 Hz, 400 µs pulse width, 5s on/5s off duty cycle), with intensity capped at a maximum of 5/10 on the pain/discomfort Visual Analog Scale (VAS).

Nutrition (In-person + Remote): High-protein (PRO) groups will focus on an intake of 1.2 to 1.5 g of protein/kg/day. Normal-protein (NOR) groups will receive general healthy eating guidelines, without encouraging an increase in protein intake.

Assessments and Outcomes (Conducted at T0 and T16)

Body Composition and Anthropometry: Multi-frequency bioelectrical impedance (InBody 570) and circumference measurements following ISAK guidelines.

Physical and Functional Performance:

Handgrip strength (dynamometry).

Muscular endurance (30-second chair stand and arm curl tests).

Upper limb power (2 kg medicine ball throw).

Aerobic endurance (6-Minute Walk Test).

Mobility and fall risk (Timed Up and Go - TUG).

Questionnaires and Scales:

Self-reported functional disability (WHODAS 2.0).

Basic psychological needs satisfaction (BPNES).

Motivational regulation in exercise (BREQ-3).

Quality of life specific for older adults (WHOQOL-OLD).

Adherence: Minimum attendance goal of 75% for the sessions.

Statistical Analysis The analysis will follow the intention-to-treat (ITT) principle. Data will be analyzed using Linear Mixed Models for Repeated Measures (fixed factors: Group and Time), followed by Tukey's post-hoc test, adopting a significance level of $p \< 0.05$.
title: WB-EMS Combined With Nutritional Guidance for a High-Protein Diet on Body Composition, Muscle Function, Psychological and Functional Outcomes in Older Adults With Excess Adiposity

brief_summary:
Ventricular tachycardia (VT) is a serious heart rhythm problem in which the heart beats very fast and in an abnormal way. These abnormal heart rhythms can be life-threatening. When a person has three or more episodes of VT within a 24-hour period, it is called a "VT storm." VT storm can be difficult to treat because some patients do not respond well to standard medications. Some studies suggest that a procedure called a stellate ganglion block (SGB) may help. An SGB involves injecting a local anesthetic near a group of nerves in the neck that help control signals between the brain and the heart. The procedure can be performed at the bedside using ultrasound guidance.

The purpose of this study is to find out whether SGB can delay or prevent the return of dangerous abnormal heart rhythms in patients with VT storm who are receiving care in an intensive care unit.

If a patient joins the study, they will be randomly assigned (by chance, like flipping a coin) to one of two groups. One group will receive a real stellate ganglion block. The other group will receive a sham procedure, in which a blunt needle will touch the skin but no injection will be given. Patients in the sham group who continue to experience VT may later receive the real procedure.

Participants will be followed until they leave the hospital or for 30 days after joining the study, whichever comes first. The study will take place at five hospitals across Ontario.
interventions: Stellate Ganglion Block Injection with Bupivicaine
primary_outcomes: Time to First Ventricular Tachycardia/Ventricular Fibrillation
title: Stellate Ganglion Neuromodulation for the Treatment of Electrical Storm: a Randomized Sham-controlled Trial

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate the effects of Ignatian Examen Meditation on students' psychological well-being, gratitude, hope, and spirituality. Specifically, it examines whether participation in Examen Meditation improves emotional well-being by reducing stress, anxiety, and depression, enhancing students' sense of gratitude and hope, and strengthening spiritual development. The study also explores the lived experiences of students and teachers who participate in the programme.

Regarding significance, this study addresses the lack of empirical studies examining Examen Meditation in Asian educational settings. The findings will provide evidence regarding the effectiveness of a Catholic contemplative practice in supporting students' mental health and spiritual formation. It may contribute to the development of school-based well-being programmes in Catholic schools by demonstrating the potential benefits of Examen Meditation for psychological well-being, the sense of gratitude and hope and spiritual growth.
primary_outcomes: The Gratitude Questionnaire - Six Item Form (GQ-6)
title: Effects of School-Based Ignatian Examen Meditation on Well-Being, Gratitude, Hope, and Spirituality in Hong Kong Catholic Primary School Students

title: The Effect of Different Intra-canal Medications on Healing of Endo-perio Cases.

brief_summary:
Objective: To investigate the failure patterns, efficacy and safety of thoracic radiotherapy combined with EGFR-TKI in stage III unresectable non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR-sensitive mutations.

Methods: This is a multicenter retrospective cohort study. Patients diagnosed with stage III unresectable EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer who received thoracic radiotherapy plus EGFR-TKI between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2024 were enrolled from five hospitals in Guangxi, including Laibin People's Hospital, The People's Hospital of Chongzuo, Liuzhou Traditional Chinese Medical Hospital, The First People's Hospital of Yulin, and The First Affiliated Hospital of Guilin Medical University. title: Thoracic Radiotherapy Plus EGFR-TKI for Stage III EGFR-mutant Lung Adenocarcinoma

Patients with persistent molecular residual disease (MRD) by tumor-informed ctDNA assay will receive consolidation chemotherapy intensification in addition to standard immunotherapy, with the goal of improving molecular response.
title: CLEAR-Lung III: Circulating Tumor DNA-Guided Consolidation Chemotherapy and Immunotherapy

brief_summary:
This prospective, cluster-randomized trial is structured as a pragmatic study, embedding the outreach intervention within routine clinical workflows. The intervention reflects real-world provider-patient communication methods. The primary research aim is to evaluate, under typical practice conditions, whether structured notification strategies improve follow-up screening.

We will evaluate whether targeted provider and patient-directed communication increases completion of CKD disease lab testing (eGFR and uACR) among individuals identified as being at risk for having CKD based on the model developed in in Phase 1. We will identify up to 1,000 patients with high risk of having CKD. All patients' primary care providers (PCPs) will receive a message notifying them of patients' elevated risk status and the recommendation for CKD testing per standard practice. Additionally, we will randomly allocate providers whose patients will receive letters ( \~n=500 patients) and providers whose patients will receive a phone call ( \~n=250 patients).
primary_outcomes: Number of days from index date (date of first provider notification) to the screening completion date by either eGFR(creatinine) or UACR, whichever comes earlier, during the follow-up period. The primary outcome will be assessed up to 12 months.
title: The Use of Risk Prediction to Identify Patients at Risk for Chronic Kidney Disease: Patient and Provider Interventions for Patients at High Risk for Chronic Kidney Disease

brief_summary:
TACTICE investigates how long-term isolation and reduced social touch during an Antarctic winter-over affect the way people perceive and respond to touch. The study will follow winter-over crew members at Concordia Station in Antarctica during the 2027 and 2028 seasons.

The study focuses on so-called C-tactile (CT) sensitivity. CT afferents are specialized nerve fibers in the skin that are known to be involved in the pleasant and regulatory effects of social touch. They may also play a role in how prolonged social isolation affects people during a long-term mission in an isolated, confined, and extreme (ICE) environment.

Participants will be assessed repeatedly before, during and after their stay. CT sensitivity will be measured using standardized touch stimulation and computer-based tasks involving touch-related stimuli. Participants will also complete questionnaires on social touch, loneliness, stress, relationships and coping. Saliva and blood samples will be collected to measure biological markers related to stress regulation and social processes, including cortisol and oxytocin.

The main hypothesis is that prolonged isolation and reduced opportunities for social touch change CT sensitivity and reduce an important source of stress regulation. These changes are expected to become more pronounced with time spent at the station and to be related to changes in stress responses, behaviour, attitudes and interpersonal functioning. The study aims to improve understanding of how people adapt to prolonged isolation and confinement and may help inform the planning of future long-duration missions in remote and extreme environments, including space missions.
primary_outcomes: Change in experiential C-tactile (CT) sensitivity assessed by pleasantness and intensity ratings on a Visual Analog Scale ranging from -10 to +10 using the Manual Tactile Stimulator.
Change in vicarious C-tactile (CT) sensitivity assessed by pleasantness and intensity ratings on a Visual Analog Scale ranging from -10 to +10 using the Vicarious Touch Task
title: The Impact of Long-term Isolation in Antarctica on Social Touch and Its Underlying Biological Mechanisms in Winter-over Crew Members, Assessed During Their Stay Using Standardized Touch Stimulation, Computer-based Touch Sensitivity Tests, Questionnaires and Biological Markers.

brief_summary:
The goal of this interventional study is to determine the effect of acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT)-based anger management training on the aggression levels of forensic psychiatry patients. The main hypotheses are:

H0: ACT-based anger management training does not affect the aggression levels of forensic psychiatry patients.

H1: ACT-based anger management training reduces the aggression levels of forensic psychiatry patients.

In the study, the researchers implemented an 8-session Acceptance and Commitment Therapy Anger Group protocol for the experimental group. The ACT training sessions were conducted once a week for a total of eight sessions. This program was applied only to the patients in the experimental group.

Both the experimental and control group patients answered the questions in the Personal Information Form, which included the patients' demographic information, and the Buss-Perry Aggression Questionnaire before and after the ACT training.

ACT-based anger management training was an effective method in reducing the aggression levels of forensic psychiatry patients.
interventions: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy-based Anger Management Training
primary_outcomes: Aggression Level Measured by the Buss-Perry Aggression Questionnaire (BPAQ)
title: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy-Based Anger Management Training in Forensic Psychiatry Patients

primary_outcomes: Number of new caries surfaces and number of progressed caries surfaces

brief_summary:
Perioperative chemotherapy with the FLOT regimen (5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin and docetaxel) is a standard treatment for resectable gastric and gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma. However, real-world studies have reported lower pathological complete response rates than the pivotal trials, and Colombian evidence is limited, coming mainly from surgical series focused on operative outcomes.

This descriptive retrospective study will review the medical records of adults with stage I to III gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma who started perioperative FLOT at Fundación Santa Fe de Bogotá (Bogotá, Colombia) between January 1, 2021 and December 31, 2025 (approximately 90 patients). It will describe pathological response (tumor regression grade by the Mandard system and pathological complete response), grade 3-4 toxicity, dose modifications, treatment adherence and completion, recurrence and overall survival. The investigators will not assign or modify any treatment, and no hypothesis testing will be performed.
title: Pathological Response to Perioperative FLOT in Gastric Adenocarcinoma

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to learn whether a structured smell training program (called "sniff training") can help improve sense of smell and quality of life in people who have experienced a reduced or lost sense of smell following a viral illness (also called post-viral anosmia).

brief_summary:
This is a Phase 2b, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiple ascending dose study designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and efficacy of TE-8105 in adults with overweight or obesity, with or without weight-related health conditions.

Participants in this study will receive subcutaneous (under the skin) injections of either TE-8105 or placebo for 25 weeks. The total study duration, including screening and follow-up visits, is approximately 8 months.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events, including treatment-related adverse events.
Changes from baseline in clinical laboratory assessments, physical examination findings, vital signs, and electrocardiogram (ECG) values.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if YJ001 Spray can treat diabetic patients with Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathic Pain(DPNP). The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is YJ001 spray effective for patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathic pain(DPNP)？
* The optimal effective dose of YJ001 spray for patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathic pain(DPNP).
* Is YJ001 spray safe for patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathic pain(DPNP)？ Researchers will divide YJ001 spray into three different doses of YJ001 spray and compare it with a placebo (a substance that looks similar but does not contain medication) to observe whether YJ001 spray can effectively treat diabetic peripheral neuropathic pain and to determine the optimal effective dose.

Participants will:

* Apply spray topically to both feet twice daily, with six sprays per foot at each administration.Attend scheduled study visits at baseline and weeks 1, 2, 4, 8, and 12, followed by a visit 1 week after Treatment termination.
* Record their symptoms and the number of times they use the spray.
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in weekly average Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) pain score at Week 12 after treatment.
title: Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, Multicenter Phase IIb Clinical Trial of Spray YJ001 for the Treatment of Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathic Pain

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to evaluate the quality of life, drug safety and therapy compliance of schizophrenia or bipolar affective disorder patients during the treatment with quetiapine monotherapy or in combination with another antipsychotic/antipsychotics. The main outcome measures are:

* quality of life using the World Health Organization Quality of Life questionnaire (WHOQOL)
* safety through the monitoring of the incidence of possible adverse drug events by the researcher, with the assessment of the association between the administration of the drug and the occurrence of an adverse reaction
* therapy adherence using the Medication Adherence Rating Scale (MARS).

The subjects will be divided into two groups:

1. Newly diagnosed patients with a diagnosis of schizophrenia or bipolar affective disorder whose individual therapeutic approach, based on the clinical assessment of the research physician, includes one of the following therapies:

   1. monotherapy with the drug quetiapine
   2. combined antipsychotic therapy with quetiapine and aripiprazole
   3. combined antipsychotic therapy with quetiapine and haloperidol
2. Patients with a diagnosis of schizophrenia or bipolar affective disorder who are on therapy with one of the antipsychotics (aripiprazole or haloperidol), and who, based on the clinical assessment of the investigator, require adjunctive quetiapine therapy. This group will include two subgroups of patients:

   1. combined antipsychotic therapy with quetiapine and aripiprazole
   2. combined antipsychotic therapy with quetiapine and haloperidol Recruitment of subjects will be carried out by physicians/researchers based on the patient's history and diagnosis. The diagnosis of schizophrenia or bipolar affective disorder will be based on the standard diagnostic criteria in medical practice (validated measurement scales in psychiatry - Young's Mania Scale, Beck Depression Scale and PANNS Schizophrenia Scale).

Patients will have four visits to physician/researcher:

1. First visit - baseline at which patient will be included in the study
2. Second visit - 4 months after the baseline
3. Third visit - 8 months after the baseline
4. Fourth visit - 12 months after the baseline
primary_outcomes: Measurement of quality of life using the World Health Organization Quality of Life questionnaire (WHOQOL)
title: Quality of Life, Safety and Compliance of Patients Using Monotherapy or Combinatorial Therapy With Quetiapine for Treatment of Schizophrenia or Bipolar Affective Disorder

brief_summary: Graves' disease is the most common cause of hyperthyroidism and is usually treated with antithyroid drugs such as methimazole (MMI). The MMI dose is adjusted according to periodic blood tests, but individual responses vary, so some patients remain hyperthyroid longer than necessary while others become hypothyroid from overtreatment. Glandy HYPER is a CE-marked, AI-based software medical device that analyzes sleep heart rate data collected by a smartwatch, together with thyroid function test results, to provide daily information on thyrotoxicosis status. This exploratory, post-market, two-center, randomized, open-label study in Germany evaluates whether MMI dose adjustment supported by Glandy HYPER shortens the time to normalization of free T4 compared with standard care, and also assesses overtreatment, thyroid-related quality of life, and safety.
primary_outcomes: Time to First Normal Free T4 Level
title: AI-Based Wearable Monitoring (Glandy HYPER) for Antithyroid Drug Dose Adjustment in Graves' Disease

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if paricalcitol or pirfenidone can help make tumors removable by surgery in adults with peritoneal cancer who are currently unable to have their tumor removed.

The study aims to answer are whether paricalcitol or pirfenidone improve tumor response and tissue healing after 12 weeks of treatment, and which of these two drugs is more effective at helping participants become eligible for surgery. Researchers will compare paricalcitol to pirfenidone to see which drug works better and has a manageable safety profile.

Participants will take either paricalcitol or pirfenidone by mouth every day for 12 weeks while continuing their standard chemotherapy, visit the clinic regularly for checkups and lab tests, keep a daily diary to track their study medication, and undergo a surgical re-evaluation after treatment to see if their tumor can be removed.
conditions: Peritoneal Carcinomatosis From Colorectal or Ovarian Origin
title: Paricalcitol Versus Pirfenidone for Improving Surgical Resectability in Patients With Peritoneal Cancer

brief_summary:
School absenteeism is a problem that can be caused by several different factors, such as difficulties within the family, problems in the school environment, or mental health difficulties. Absenteeism can, in turn, lead to negative consequences such as poorer mental health, social isolation, and long-term difficulties later in life. For children, school absenteeism has negative consequences for their education, social relationships, and important daily routines-routines that can otherwise serve as a protective factor against, among other things, mental health difficulties, particularly for children in vulnerable environments (Selman, 2023). It is therefore important that problems are identified at an early stage and that schools, parents, and pupils work together to reduce absenteeism (Kearney, 2008; Gren-Landell, 2021).

About EAGLE EAGLE (Earle Absenteeism Guide for Lifelong Education) is a collaborative model between schools and families aimed at preventing school absenteeism at an early stage, before absenteeism becomes extensive and therefore more difficult to address. Primary schools are organisations with limited resources and a need for simple, practically oriented working methods. EAGLE therefore has a simple basic structure, with the aim of being implemented quickly when pupils begin to show problematic absenteeism.

Here, problematic absenteeism refers to absenteeism that is caused by something in the child's life that is not functioning well or needs to change-for example, difficulties at school, at home, or in everyday life-and not by a straightforward cause such as a common cold. The target group is children in the early and middle years of primary school. An important component is to strengthen collaboration between parents and school staff, as well as to provide parents with guidance on parenting in relation to the child's difficulties attending school.

The Gradual Development of Absenteeism Absenteeism does not begin from one day to the next; rather, it develops gradually. Unfortunately, it is common for interventions to be introduced only when absenteeism has become extensive, by which point it is more difficult to reverse. EAGLE, on the other hand, is implemented earlier, increasing the possibility of, so to speak, turning the ship in the right direction and helping children and parents establish a positive experience of school attendance.

In brief, EAGLE consists of three collaborative meetings between the school and the child's parent(s)/guardian(s), two sessions providing psychological guidance to the parents, and two shorter conversations with the child to obtain their perspective. The basic principle is that, when it comes to school absenteeism among young children under the age of 12, adults-both at school and at home-should collaborate and drive the change, rather than placing this responsibility on the child. Nevertheless, the child's perspective must be taken into account throughout the entire process.

School absenteeism is often described as a complex phenomenon involving an interaction between different factors that mutually influence one another (Swedish National Agency for Education, 2021). These factors may vary, but they generally concern three main areas: 1) school-related factors, 2) individual-related factors, and 3) family-related factors. The EAGLE working model provides a method for mapping these three areas and subsequently implementing appropriate interventions. Considerable time is devoted to establishing good collaboration between the school and the family and to helping parents manage the difficulties that arise when a child does not want to attend school.

Aim

The research project aims to:

Evaluate the effectiveness of the EAGLE intervention. Understand which factors influence children's absenteeism, including factors related to both parents and pupils.

Materials and Methods The research project will use both qualitative and quantitative data. The primary outcome measure will be school attendance.

We will also investigate factors in the child's life that may influence absenteeism, such as symptoms of anxiety and depression, as well as their parents' attitudes towards school based on their own experiences as children.
title: Early Absenteeism Guide for Lifelong Education

brief_summary: This study uses FES PET/CT imaging to evaluate estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer. The purpose of this study is to see how well FES PET/CT can help doctors: (1) diagnose ER-positive breast cancer, (2) plan the best treatment, and (3) check how well treatment is working. Participants will undergo FES PET/CT scans as part of their regular cancer care or study procedures. The results may help improve how doctors use imaging to guide treatment decisions for patients with ER-positive breast cancer.
title: 18F-FES PET/CT in the Treatment Planning, and Response Assessment of ER-Positive Breast Cancer

brief_summary: Primary objective is to compare isolated single tunnel transtibial pull out posterior medial meniscus root repair (PMMRR) with the same repair augmented by arthroscopic capsulodesis. Study design: Prospective randomized controlled trial. The study will be registered in the international Clinical Trials registry. Inclusion criteria: symptomatic isolated PMMRT confirmed by MRI, type 2 or type 4 tears according to the LaPrade classification, age between 18 and 65 years, neutral coronal alignment (mechanical axis deviation \<4° varus), as confirmed on standardized full-length standing radiographs. Exclusion criteria: previous ipsilateral meniscal or ligament surgery, body mass index (BMI) \>35 kg/m², advanced osteoarthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence grade III-IV), inflammatory arthropathy, metabolic bone disease, spontaneous osteonecrosis of the knee or inability to adhere to the standardized postoperative rehabilitation protocol. Randomization: Eligible patients will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to either isolated posterior medial meniscus root repair group (PMMRR) or PMMRR augmented with arthroscopic capsulodesis group, performed centrally by an independent statistician using a computer-generated randomization sequence with variable block sizes of 4 to 6. Image control with MRI will be performed at 3, 6 and 12 month and evaluated by two fellowship-trained musculoskeletal radiologists blinded to treatment allocation, clinical information, and temporal sequence of scans.The primary endpoint (medial meniscal extrusion at 12 months) will be analyzed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), with treatment group as the fixed effect, baseline extrusion as a covariate, and study center included as a random effect to account for clustering.
lead_sponsor: Institut Català de Traumatologia i Medicina de l'Esport
title: Arthroscopic Capsulodesis Decreases Meniscal Extrusion at 1 Year Follow up When Combined With Transtibial Pull Out Repair of Posteromedial Root Lesion. A Prospective Randomized Study

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to assess, in a clinical setting, the efficacy and the safety of FLEXIPORT, a totally implantable venous access device (TIVAD) designed to provide a repeated access to the vascular system, in patients with malignant diseases requiring central venous access for administration of chemotherapeutic treatments. brief_summary:
Postoperative sleep disturbance is common in patients undergoing gynecologic surgery and may affect postoperative recovery. This prospective observational cohort study will evaluate perioperative EEG changes in patients undergoing gynecologic laparoscopic surgery and examine their association with postoperative sleep disturbance.

Approximately 300 adult patients will be enrolled. Frontal EEG will be recorded during the perioperative period, and relevant clinical information will be collected. Postoperative sleep and recovery will be assessed using standardized questionnaires. EEG features and clinical variables will then be analyzed to determine which factors are associated with postoperative sleep disturbance and whether their combination can be used for early risk prediction.

The study is intended to characterize perioperative EEG features associated with postoperative sleep disturbance and to develop a clinically applicable risk prediction model. No study-specific treatment or intervention will be assigned to participants.
lead_sponsor: General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to learn about the outcomes, usability, and accessibility of the online Brain Health Pro program for older adults with hearing difficulties, vision difficulties, or both. Brain Health Pro (BHPro) provides information and practical suggestions about ways people may support their brain health and lower their risk of dementia.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Does participants' knowledge about dementia and its risk factors change after using Brain Health Pro? How usable and accessible is Brain Health Pro for people with hearing or vision difficulties? What factors help or make it more difficult for participants to use and complete the program?

About 300 adults aged 55 years and older with hearing difficulties, vision difficulties, or both will take part in the study. Participants will:

Use the online Brain Health Pro program for six months. Complete online questionnaires before starting the program and again at 3 and 6 months.

Share their experiences using the program, including any difficulties related to hearing, vision, or using the online program.

Researchers will also look at whether participants make changes in health behaviours that may support brain health and whether they feel more confident about making these changes.
primary_outcomes: Change in Knowledge About Alzheimer's Disease Assessed Using the Alzheimer's Disease Knowledge Scale (ADKS)
title: SENSE-Brain Health Pro for Older Adults With Sensory Loss

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate inflammatory biomarkers associated with suicide risk and to evaluate the efficacy of videoconference-based brief cognitive-behavioral therapy (V-BCBT) in patients with mood disorders at high risk for suicide. The study consists of a cross-sectional baseline comparison followed by a randomized controlled trial.

Participants will include patients with depressive disorders or bipolar and related disorders who are experiencing a major depressive episode, as well as healthy controls with no lifetime history of DSM-5 psychiatric disorders. Patients with mood disorders will be classified as being at high or low risk for suicide. At baseline, all participants, including those in the high-suicide-risk, low-suicide-risk, and healthy control groups, will undergo clinical interviews, self-report questionnaires, a computer-based Death Implicit Association Test (D-IAT), and blood sampling. Clinical characteristics and inflammatory biomarker profiles will be compared across the three groups to examine the potential utility of inflammatory biomarkers for identifying individuals at high risk for suicide.

Participants in the high-suicide-risk group who meet all eligibility criteria will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to V-BCBT plus treatment as usual (TAU) or TAU alone. For participants in the high-suicide-risk group, the baseline assessment will also serve as the pre-treatment assessment and will be conducted within 7 days before the start of treatment. V-BCBT consists of eight individual sessions of approximately 50-60 minutes, delivered once weekly via secure videoconferencing by trained therapists. The intervention includes crisis management, development of a suicide-focused coping plan, exploration of reasons for living, relaxation training, behavioral activation, cognitive restructuring, mindfulness, coping strategies for high-risk situations, and relapse prevention. TAU consists of routine outpatient psychiatric care and may include pharmacotherapy and supportive psychotherapy.

Participants in the high-suicide-risk group will subsequently undergo a post-treatment assessment at 2 months after the baseline assessment (±7 days) and a follow-up assessment at 2 months after the post-treatment assessment (±10 days). The post-treatment and follow-up assessments will include clinical interviews, self-report questionnaires, the D-IAT, and blood sampling. Participants in the low-suicide-risk and healthy control groups will complete the baseline assessment only and will not undergo post-treatment or follow-up assessments. Post-treatment and follow-up clinical assessments of randomized participants will be conducted by evaluators blinded to treatment allocation.
primary_outcomes: Number of Suicide Attempts Assessed Using the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS)
Time to First Suicide Attempt Following Treatment Assessed Using the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS)
Baseline Differences in Serum Inflammatory Biomarker Levels Measured by Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA)
Change in Serum Inflammatory Biomarker Levels Measured by Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA)
title: Videoconference-Based Brief Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Patients With Mood Disorders at High Risk for Suicide

brief_summary:
Several health care professions use manual therapy techniques (joint manipulation and mobilization, and soft tissue treatment) to successfully treat back and neck pain. However, it is still unknown how manual techniques work. As with any type of treatment, there are at least two possible explanations. First, the treatment might cause physical changes in the body; for manual therapy, these would be changes in the joints, muscles, or other tissues. Second, patients might feel better because they believe the treatment will help. In drug trials, it is relatively easy to determine the extent to which patients' beliefs contribute to treatment effects: patients can be given a dummy pill with no active ingredient (a "placebo"). In this way, patients are "blinded," meaning that they do not know whether they received the real drug or not. In manual therapy studies, however, blinding is difficult because patients can feel whether or not they are receiving real treatment. This problem can be overcome by sedating patients: while asleep, patients receive either real hands-on manual therapy or no treatment. Because patients do not know which treatment they received, it becomes possible to determine whether any benefits result from changes in the body or from patients' expectations.

In this pilot study, 20 participants with low back or neck pain lasting at least three months will be sedated for approximately 15 minutes. Half of them (the "true group") will receive manual therapy to the spine. The other half (the "sham group") will be sedated for the same length of time but will not receive any treatment. Before and after the intervention, and again at a follow-up visit two weeks later, spinal mobility will be assessed and blood samples will be collected to measure substances known to change after spinal manipulative therapy. At these time points, and again at three and six months, participants will complete questionnaires about their pain, how much the pain limits them, any side effects they notice, which treatment they believe they received, and how they experienced the intervention and the period that followed.

The purpose of this pilot study is twofold. First, the study will assess whether enough participants can be recruited and retained for the full study duration, and whether they remain unaware of their group allocation. If participants correctly guess which group they were in, this would indicate that they were not truly blinded. Second, preliminary data from the questionnaires, mobility tests, and blood samples will be collected to explore potential differences between the true and sham groups. These results will help in designing a larger follow-up study, which is planned if this pilot study is successful. Such a study could then determine whether manual therapy works through physiological changes in the body, through patient expectations, or through a combination of both. Participants in this pilot study may benefit directly through reduced pain and/or improved spinal mobility. More broadly, the knowledge gained from this pilot study may ultimately lead to improved treatments and better clinical outcomes for patients with spinal pain.
primary_outcomes: Feasibility will be assessed based on the recruitment rate
Feasibility will be also assessed based on success of participant blinding
Feasibility will be also assessed based on Adverse events
Feasibility will be also assessed based on Loss to follow-up
title: Spinal Manual Therapy Under Sedation

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to determine if prophylactic silver-nylon burn dressing Silverlon® prevents a severe skin reaction under tracheostomy collars. It also aims to establish whether patients can tolerate Silverlon® under their tracheostomy with daily removal and weekly changes.

Families are recruited from specialized palliative care units in the Stockholm region by health care social workers during 2024-2025. FTI consists of six meetings with the family (the whole family and each family member separately) after about 3-4 months after death of a parent. Follow-up interviews with bereaved family members over the age of 6 are conducted, face-to-face or digitally. brief_summary: In terms of blood flow per unit of tissue, the retina is one of the tissues with the highest blood flow in the body. Parameters such as the thickness of the choroid layer, which plays a crucial role in maintaining normal eye function, the dimensions of the foveal avascular zone (FAZ) supplied by this layer, and retinal vascular networks can be measured using non-invasive methods. OCTA (Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography) is an imaging tool that enables the non-invasive assessment of retinal microvascular densities and the measurement of the foveal avascular zone's dimensions. Studies conducted to date indicate that retinal capillary vessels and the dimensions of the foveal avascular zone are affected in rheumatological diseases, especially associated with systemic inflammation. This study aims to compare retinal capillary vessel density and foveal avascular zone dimensions in patients with psoriatic arthritis against those in a healthy population and in patients with psoriasis who do not have psoriatic arthritis, utilizing the non-invasive method of optical coherence tomography angiography.

brief_summary:
Postoperative delirium is a frequent complication after cardiac surgery. This prospective observational study will evaluate whether cerebral blood flow velocity measured by transcranial Doppler before and during elective heart valve surgery is associated with delirium during the first five postoperative days. Bispectral index, near-infrared spectroscopy, and arterial blood gas data will also be recorded. Delirium will be assessed daily by an independent evaluator who is blinded to the intraoperative measurements and artificial intelligence predictions, using CAM-ICU for mechanically ventilated patients or the Turkish 3D-CAM for patients on the ward.

The study will also compare zero-shot delirium risk predictions from five general-purpose large language models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, and Kimi) with the blinded clinical assessments. The models will not be trained on data from the study cohort.
title: Transcranial Doppler and Artificial Intelligence Prediction of Postoperative Delirium in Heart Valve Surgery

brief_summary:
Engage-PD is a single cohort evaluation of implementation of a telehealth-delivered physical activity coaching program for people with early-mid stage Parkinson's disease in Spanish population. The program utilizes a physiotherapist to provide one-on-one coaching for individuals with early-mid stage Parkinson's disease to provide individualized structured support to facilitate and optimize exercise uptake as part of an effective self-management program.

BACKGROUND: Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative condition for which there is currently no cure. Physical activity and exercise have demonstrated benefits for motor and non-motor symptoms, functional performance, and brain structure and function. Exercise, particularly at higher intensities, may also provide neuroprotective and neurorestorative effects and may be especially important during the early stages of the disease. Despite these potential benefits, people with Parkinson's disease are substantially less active than healthy adults, and physical activity declines as the disease progresses. Perceived barriers, including low expectations of exercise benefits, limited time, fear of falling, and lack of motivation, may contribute to reduced participation. Despite this, there is limited research examining interventions specifically designed to increase and maintain aerobic exercise.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to investigate the feasibility and acceptability of a theory-based behavioural change program designed to increase aerobic exercise participation in Spanish population. The study will also examine whether the intervention can improve exercise self-efficacy and motivation and reduce perceived barriers to physical activity.

METHODOLOGY: A single cohort of people with Parkinson's disease in the stages of Hoehn and Yahr I-III who are willing to participate in the 3-month Engage-PD program, which consisted of up to 5 telehealth coaching sessions delivered by a trained physical therapist expert in Parkinson's disease. Feasibility is evaluated based on recruitment and retention rates, along with participants' feedback. Planned and unplanned physical activity, exercise self-efficacy, and individualized goals are assessed pre- and post-intervention. Relationships between baseline characteristics and changes in planned PA and ESE are also evaluated.

SIGNIFICANCE: A behavioural change program that integrates instrumental, emotional, and informational support may help individuals with early-stage Parkinson's disease establish sustainable exercise habits and incorporate physical activity into daily routines. Physiotherapists may play an important role in supporting these behavioural changes by addressing physical performance, self-management, cognitive-behavioural strategies, and environmental factors that influence participation in exercise.
title: Engage-PD: a Physical Activity Coaching Program Via Telehealth for People With Parkinson's Disease. A Single-cohort Study in Spain.

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to show that there is no difference in patient clinical scores when patients with knee pain are treated with joint application of high dose white blood cell PRP (platelet-rich plasma) and low dose white blood cell PRP for knee osteoarthritis. Before being recruited, they will undergo radiological examinations (X-ray and MRI), based on which they will be recruited. Before application and subjection to randomization, all patients will fill out clinical questionnaires (KOOS,WOMAC,VAS). Afterwards, the participants will be divided randomly into two groups, one receiving high dose white blood cell PRP and the other group receiving low dose white blood cell PRP. brief_summary:
A significant proportion of patients remain resistant to antidepressant therapies, even when treatment is well managed. Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is a well-established method for treating certain severe and resistant psychiatric pathologies. ECT is also the gold standard for treating mood disorders. Although effective, it is associated with cognitive side effects (memory impairment, post-ECT confusion, longer reorientation time), particularly with bitemporal (BT) montage and brief pulse stimulation. These effects may contribute to patient reluctance and limit adherence to this therapy. From a mechanistic point of view, ECT causes changes in cerebral blood flow (rCBF) and brain electrical activity, particularly in the prefrontal cortex, where the induction of "pseudo-epileptic seizures" appears to be related to therapeutic efficacy, while cognitive side effects appear to be associated with alterations in the temporal areas. The conventional stimulation method results in widespread diffusion of the current due to the properties of the skull, limiting control over the distribution of intracerebral charge densities. In this context, a new approach called "Focal Electrically Administered Seizure Therapy" (FEAST) has been developed to focus the electrical current and limit cognitive side effects. Unlike traditional ECT, FEAST uses unidirectional current and optimized electrode placement, aiming to induce seizures in a more localized manner in the right prefrontal cortex while reducing propagation to temporal regions.

The FEAST configuration is based on scientific literature (protocols, parameters, electrode positioning) and not on a "pre configured" mode validated by the medical device manufacturer.

Neuroimaging studies suggest that FEAST causes an increase in blood flow in the right prefrontal cortex at the onset of the seizure, followed by a postictal redistribution similar to that observed with ECT, confirming its targeted effect. Open-label clinical trials conducted to date show that FEAST significantly improves depressive symptoms with a more favorable cognitive profile compared to traditional ECT, notably by reducing the impact on autobiographical memory and decreasing the time needed to regain orientation acutely after treatment. Several comparative studies between FEAST and unilateral ultra-brief pulse ECT suggest an advantage in terms of cognitive tolerance, although the differences are not always statistically significant. A multicenter trial also showed comparable effects on reducing suicidal ideation, suggesting that FEAST could be an alternative to traditional ECT. Indeed, preliminary studies indicate that FEAST may offer similar benefits to ECT in terms of reducing depressive symptoms, but with fewer cognitive side effects, which could lead to a better quality of life.

Although these studies are promising, they remain few in number and have methodological limitations (open-label clinical trials, feasibility studies, lack of randomization with a comparator arm, small sample size, or assignment to the study arm based on patient preference). There are currently no other randomized clinical trials on FEAST underway or in preparation worldwide. Well-designed, multicenter clinical trials with sufficient patient numbers to achieve satisfactory statistical power are therefore needed to address the limitations of previous studies and explore the clinical benefits of FEAST.

The present study is therefore a randomized, multicenter, double-blind clinical trial designed to evaluate the superiority of FEAST in terms of safety and efficacy compared to traditional ECT modalities.
