brief_summary:
The purpose of this randomized clinical trial is to compare two surgical methods for removing enlarged adenoids in children: conventional curettage adenoidectomy and endoscopic microdebrider-assisted adenoidectomy. Enlarged adenoids can cause problems such as snoring, mouth breathing, obstructive sleep apnea, and changes in facial appearance.

The main question this study aims to answer is:

* Does endoscopic microdebrider-assisted adenoidectomy result in different operative outcomes compared with conventional curettage adenoidectomy?

The study will include 88 children aged 3-16 years who have enlarged adenoids and symptoms such as obstructive sleep apnea, mouth breathing, or snoring. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups:

* Group A: Adenoidectomy using a conventional adenoid curette.
* Group B: Adenoidectomy using a microdebrider while viewing the adenoids with an endoscope.

All procedures will be performed under general anesthesia. The researchers will record the duration of the operation and the amount of blood lost during surgery. These outcomes will be compared between the two groups to determine whether the surgical techniques differ in operative time and blood loss.

Parents or guardians will provide informed consent before their child participates in the study.
title: Conventional Curettage Versus Endoscopic Microdebrider-Assisted Adenoidectomy in Children

brief_summary:
Family caregivers of people living with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias often experience conflicts and communication challenges when coordinating care, making decisions, and interacting with family members and healthcare providers. These challenges can contribute to caregiver burden, stress, anxiety, and reduced well-being.

The purpose of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness of NegotiAge, an online negotiation and communication training program designed for family caregivers. NegotiAge provides education and interactive practice exercises to help caregivers develop negotiation, problem-solving, conflict-resolution, and communication skills that can be applied to real-world caregiving situations.

Approximately 200 family caregivers will be randomly assigned to either the NegotiAge intervention or an attention-control educational website. Participants will complete online surveys before the intervention, immediately after the intervention, and at 1-month and 3-month follow-up time-points. The study will examine whether NegotiAge reduces caregiver burden and improves communication, conflict-management behaviors, self-efficacy, stress, anxiety, fatigue, and well-being. Findings from this research may help improve support programs for family caregivers of people living with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias.
primary_outcomes: Change in Zarit Caregiver Burden Score

brief_summary:
Chronic hypoparathyroidism is a rare condition in which the parathyroid glands do not make enough parathyroid hormone (PTH). PTH helps control the levels of calcium and phosphate in the blood. When there is not enough PTH, calcium levels can become too low and phosphate levels can become too high. This may cause symptoms such as tingling, muscle cramps, weakness, or other health problems.

The most common cause of chronic hypoparathyroidism is surgery in the neck area. It can happen after thyroid surgery, surgery on the parathyroid glands, or other operations in the neck.

At the moment, most patients are treated with calcium and vitamin D tablets. These treatments help control calcium levels, but they cannot fully replace the normal effects of PTH in the body. A medicine that contains a form of human PTH is available for some patients, but it is not yet the standard treatment for everyone.

This registry collects medical information and follows patients over time. Its aim is to better understand patients' symptoms, possible long-term health problems, treatments, and overall health. A group of patients who have had their thyroid removed but do not have hypoparathyroidism will also be included for comparison.
title: German Hypoparathyroidism Registry

brief_summary:
The SPECTRA-HFpEF Study is a randomized, double-blind, Phase 2 clinical study designed to evaluate and compare the biological effects of vicadrostat in combination with empagliflozin, empagliflozin alone, and spironolactone in combination with empagliflozin in adults with heart failure and preserved ejection fraction. The study will enroll approximately 200 participants with chronic heart failure, New York Heart Association Class II to IV symptoms, and left ventricular ejection fraction greater than 40%. The primary objective is to determine whether treatment with vicadrostat/empagliflozin produces differential changes in circulating plasma proteins compared with spironolactone/empagliflozin, using a broad proteomic panel measured over the course of treatment. These proteomic changes may help identify biological pathways affected by each treatment strategy, including pathways related to inflammation, myocardial fibrosis and remodeling, kidney function, cardiac stress, and aldosterone-related signaling.

Participants will complete an approximately 26-week study period, including screening, treatment, and follow-up phases. After screening and any required washout of prior sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor therapy, participants will receive open-label empagliflozin and will be randomized in a blinded manner to receive vicadrostat or placebo during the first treatment period. During the second treatment period, participants will receive either continued vicadrostat with empagliflozin or spironolactone with empagliflozin. During the third treatment period, vicadrostat or spironolactone will be discontinued while empagliflozin is continued. Blood and urine samples will be collected at specified visits to evaluate changes in proteomic markers, renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system biomarkers, collagen turnover markers, sex hormone markers, kidney function, proteinuria, inflammatory biomarkers, and cardiac stress biomarkers. Echocardiography and patient-reported health status assessments will also be performed to explore potential effects on cardiac structure, function, symptoms, and quality of life.

The study is intended to improve understanding of how aldosterone synthase inhibition with vicadrostat differs from mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism with spironolactone when each is used with empagliflozin in patients with heart failure and preserved ejection fraction. By comparing treatment-related proteomic and biomarker changes across study arms, the study may provide insight into mechanistic differences between these therapeutic approaches and help inform future development of targeted combination therapies for heart failure. Safety and tolerability will be monitored throughout the study through collection of adverse events, serious adverse events, vital signs, electrocardiograms, physical examinations, and clinical laboratory assessments, including kidney function and serum potassium monitoring.
conditions: Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFPEF)
primary_outcomes: Differences in the proteomic regulation following Treatment Period 2
title: This Will be a Randomized Comparison of the Proteomic Effects of Vicadrostat/Empagliflozin Versus Empagliflozin and Versus Empagliflozin/Spironolactone in Heart Failure Patients With Preserved Ejection Fraction

Favorable effects of the Mediterranean diet on numerous diseases have been confirmed in clinical research, but in the case of ulcerative colitis, there is a lack of well-designed studies.

The aim of this study is to demonstrate that a modified Mediterranean diet (MMD) with reduced carbohydrate intake over a duration of 12 weeks, in conjunction with standard therapy, has a favorable impact on symptoms and objective markers of inflammation in ulcerative colitis patients.

brief_summary:
Anal canal cancer is primarily associated with persistent infection by high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV), particularly HPV-16. Women who have undergone solid organ transplantation are at increased risk of anal cancer because of the chronic immunosuppression required to maintain graft function. However, epidemiological data regarding the prevalence of anal HPV-16 and other HR-HPV types in this population remain limited and sometimes conflicting.

EPAHTOS is a single-center, cross-sectional, observational study (French Category 2 Interventional Research Involving Human Participants \[RIPH 2\]) conducted at Montpellier University Hospital. The study aims to evaluate the prevalence of anal HPV-16 carriage among women aged 18 to 75 years who underwent kidney, liver, and/or heart transplantation more than 10 years previously, or who have received cumulative immunosuppressive therapy for more than 10 years. A total of 190 participants will be enrolled.

At the inclusion visit, participants will receive information about the study, provide written informed consent, complete a self-administered questionnaire including questions on HPV infection risk factors, and perform a self-collected anal sample for the detection of high-risk HPV by polymerase chain reaction (PCR). This test allows identification of HPV-16 as well as other HR-HPV genotypes.

The primary objective is to estimate the prevalence of anal HPV-16 carriage. Secondary objectives include assessing the distribution of other anal HR-HPV genotypes, describing cytological abnormalities associated with HR-HPV infections, estimating the prevalence of anal histological lesions detected by high-resolution anoscopy among eligible participants, identifying factors associated with HR-HPV carriage, evaluating the feasibility of anal self-sampling, and describing the distribution of cervical HR-HPV infections.

In accordance with French recommendations, participants testing positive for HPV-16 will receive standard clinical management including reflex anal cytology and, in the event of a cytological abnormality, referral for proctology consultation with high-resolution anoscopy. Within the framework of the study, participants carrying an HR-HPV genotype other than HPV-16 and presenting abnormal cytology will also be offered standard proctological evaluation to ensure that clinically significant anal lesions are not overlooked.

The results of this study will provide updated information on the epidemiology of HPV infections among female solid organ transplant recipients and may contribute to the development of future anal cancer screening strategies in this high-risk population.
interventions: Anal Self-Sampling for High-Risk HPV Detection
title: Epidemiology of Anal Human Papillomavirus Carriage in Female Solid Organ Transplant Recipients With More Than 10 Years of Immunosuppression

brief_summary: This study evaluated the validity and reliability of the Turkish version of the Intuitive Eating Scale-2 (IES-2) in individuals who had undergone bariatric surgery and examined the effects of a 6-week online intuitive eating intervention. The study consisted of two stages. In the first stage, 297 adults aged 18-65 years who had undergone bariatric surgery were included to evaluate the psychometric properties of the Turkish IES-2. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, internal consistency, and test-retest reliability were assessed. In the second stage, a 6-week prospective, non-randomized controlled intervention study was conducted among 60 individuals who had undergone bariatric surgery at least two years previously and had regained at least 20% of their maximum weight loss. Participants received either an online intuitive eating intervention or standard nutritional counseling. Outcomes included intuitive eating behaviors, eating attitudes, body perception, body weight, and body mass index (BMI). The Turkish IES-2 demonstrated a valid and reliable three-factor, 17-item structure. The intervention was associated with improvements in intuitive eating behaviors and reductions in eating attitude scores, while no significant changes were observed in body weight or BMI. The findings suggest that an online intuitive eating intervention may improve intuitive eating behaviors and some eating attitudes among individuals who regain weight after bariatric surgery.
conditions: Weight Regain After Bariatric Surgery and Food Addiction
title: Intuitive Eating Intervention After Bariatric Surgery

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial aims to investigate the effects of preoperative video-assisted patient education combined with eye position fixation training on anxiety, pain, intraoperative compliance, operation duration, and physiological parameters in adult patients undergoing primary pterygium surgery under local anesthesia. A total of 152 patients aged 18 to 75 years scheduled for primary pterygium excision with conjunctival autograft will be randomly assigned to either the intervention group (n = 76) or the control group (n = 76). Patients in the intervention group will receive an 8-to-10-minute tablet-based audiovisual surgical preparation module prior to surgery. This module consists of two stages: (1) cognitive preparation based on Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) principles, including 2D animations of the procedure, desensitization to operating room sights and sounds, and postoperative care instructions; and (2) interactive eye position fixation and motor compliance training. Patients in the control group will receive standard routine verbal preoperative information. Anxiety levels, pain intensity, and physiological parameters (blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation) will be assessed preoperatively and postoperatively. Intraoperative patient compliance and surgical comfort will be evaluated immediately after surgery by a blinded surgeon, along with total operation duration and intraoperative physiological parameters.
title: Video-Assisted Patient Education and Eye Fixation Training in Pterygium Surgery

brief_summary:
The protocol the investigators propose aims to address certain gaps by developing a multimodal paradigm, based on:

* Induction of acute stress via the Maastricht Acute Stress Test (MAST), a standardised protocol recognised for its effectiveness in activating both the HPA axis and the autonomic nervous system.
* A 10-minute auditory exposure to two types of soundscapes (natural vs urban), designed in accordance with ecological standards (recordings taken from real-world environments and featuring representative natural and anthropogenic sound components, with the aim of making the stimulus as close as possible to real-life experiences).
* A battery of synchronised, multimodal measurements, including hormonal measurements (salivary cortisol at 10 time points), continuous autonomic nervous system measurements (HR, HRV, BP), a high-density EEG and analysis via EEG Source Imaging (ESI), a battery of cognitive tests typically sensitive to stress (Continuous Visual Attention Task, N-back, Delay Discounting Task), and a light polysomnography study conducted at home to assess delayed effects on sleep.

This design will enable the investigators to examine, as comprehensively as possible, the dynamics of post-stress recovery across several levels of analysis (biological, cerebral, cognitive and behavioural). It will also enable the investigators to identify the specific effects of the sound environment on each of these levels. By cross-referencing neurophysiological, hormonal and behavioural responses, we hope to document how natural sound environments actively regulate stress and cognition and to explore the mechanisms involved.

This project could pave the way for applications in mental health, preventive neuroscience, acoustic urban planning and non-pharmacological interventions, by providing a rigorous scientific foundation to support recommendations for the design or management of stress in professional, educational or clinical settings.
primary_outcomes: Change in salivary cortisol concentration following acute stress and a natural soundscape exposure.
Change in salivary cortisol concentration following acute stress and an urban soundscape exposure.
title: Stress Through Audition: Uptake, Recovery, Oscillations During Nature Exposure

brief_summary:
Adjuvant hormonotherapy is a cornerstone of treatment for localized hormone receptor-positive (HR+) breast cancer, accounting for approximately 80% of patients. The main classes used are selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs, including tamoxifen) and aromatase inhibitors (anastrozole, letrozole, exemestane), with or without LH-RH agonists (leuprorelin, goserelin), administered daily for 5 to 8 years.

However, these treatments are frequently associated with adverse events, predominantly musculoskeletal disorders such as arthralgia, which can significantly impair quality of life. These symptoms cause functional impact and promote premature discontinuation of treatment, thereby compromising therapeutic adherence and increasing the risk of tumor relapse.

Current management strategies for these arthralgias, whether pharmacological or non-pharmacological, show limited efficacy or insufficient levels of evidence, with the exception of certain approaches like acupuncture. In the absence of satisfactory solutions, many patients turn to alternative medicines, notably phytotherapy. However, these practices raise safety concerns (drug interactions, misuse) and rely on limited scientific evidence, especially since they are often underreported to healthcare professionals.

In this context, there is a clear need to rigorously evaluate new therapeutic approaches. The non-randomized ERABLE study aims to explore the efficacy and acceptability of a phytotherapy selected for its analgesic properties on hormone therapy-induced arthralgia in patients treated for localized breast cancer. If positive, this study will be followed by a randomized trial to confirm efficacy and achieve a level of evidence compatible with clinical guidelines.
interventions: Phytotherapy Dietary Supplement (Harpagophytum, Meadowsweet, and Blackcurrant)
primary_outcomes: Change in joint pain score from baseline to day 21
title: Evaluation of the Efficacy and Acceptability of a Phytotherapy Combining Devil's Claw, Blackcurrant and Meadowsweet for the Management of Aromatase Inhibitor-induced Arthralgia in Patients Treated for Localized Breast Cancer in the Adjuvant Setting

brief_summary:
Patients with BMI 60 kg/m² or higher are the hardest operations in bariatric surgery. Thick abdominal wall, massive hepatomegaly, reduced working space, fragile fatty tissue, higher conversion and complication rates. Every bariatric surgeon knows this group. Almost no trial recruits it.

The standard answer is a short liver-reduction diet before surgery. It helps, but the effect is modest, hard to tolerate, and short-lived. GLP-1-based drugs now produce far larger and better-tolerated weight loss and are already being given before surgery in routine practice, without trial evidence. Retrospective series show more preoperative weight loss and no obvious harm, and no more than that (Obesity Research \& Clinical Practice 2026). A 2023 review of drugs on the surgical waiting list found that GLP-1 receptor agonists had never been evaluated for the preoperative indication at all.

Two registered trials are now adjacent to this question, and we cite both. The PreMO pilot randomizes 50 patients to open-label preoperative tirzepatide versus standard care, with tissue inflammation as the scientific focus (PMID 41643256; NCT06721507). A three-arm trial before one-anastomosis gastric bypass compares tirzepatide, ketogenic diet, and standard care, with weight loss at one year as primary (NCT07622992). Neither is blinded. Neither recruits BMI 60 and above. Neither measures whether the drug actually makes the operation easier and safer. The 2024 IFSO international consensus reached 100% agreement that evidence is insufficient to recommend routine preoperative medication, that use must be individualized, and that more research on benefits, risks, and outcomes is required; it also agreed, at 97%, that adequate protein and resistance exercise must accompany any preoperative drug treatment (PMID 39612579). This trial is the research that consensus calls for, and its preoperative program is built to the 97% requirement.
lead_sponsor: General Committee of Teaching Hospitals and Institutes, Egypt
title: Semaglutide Before Primary Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery in Patients With BMI 60 kg/m² or Higher

brief_summary:
\### What is this study about?

This study looked at whether adding \*\*pain neuroscience education (PNE)\*\* to standard therapeutic exercise helps people with chronic low back pain who are afraid of moving (a condition called \*kinesiophobia\*).

\### Why does it matter?

Chronic low back pain is the leading cause of disability worldwide. Many people with chronic back pain develop fear of movement, which makes them avoid exercise and can slow down recovery. While exercise is the recommended first-line treatment, fear of movement often reduces how much patients benefit from it.

Pain neuroscience education is a talking therapy that helps patients understand that chronic pain is not always a sign of tissue damage - it often involves the nervous system becoming overly sensitive. The idea is that changing how patients think about pain may reduce their fear and help them engage more fully in exercise.

\### What did the researchers do?

Patients with chronic low back pain and high fear of movement were randomly assigned to two groups

* \*\*Group 1:\*\* 8 weeks of therapeutic exercise alone
* \*\*Group 2:\*\* 8 weeks of therapeutic exercise \*\*plus\*\* two pain neuroscience education sessions (at the start and at week 4)
* Patients were assessed at \*\*baseline, 8 weeks, and 24 weeks\*\* (6-month follow-up)
* Measures included: fear of movement (TSK-17), pain intensity (NRS), disability (RMDQ), pain catastrophizing (PCS), and central sensitization symptoms (CSI)
* Brain scans (resting-state fMRI) were taken before and after the intervention to explore potential brain-behavior links
title: Therapeutic Exercise Plus Pain Neuroscience Education for Chronic Low Back Pain

brief_summary:
Endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) is increasingly performed under local anesthesia with intravenous sedation, but the optimal sedative agent has not been established. Dexmedetomidine provides cooperative sedation with minimal respiratory depression and may have renoprotective effects, whereas propofol is widely used but can cause respiratory depression and hypotension.

This single-center retrospective cohort study compares dexmedetomidine-based and propofol-based sedation in adult patients who underwent EVAR under local anesthesia and sedation at Bursa City Hospital. The primary outcome is postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) defined by KDIGO serum creatinine criteria. Secondary outcomes include intensive care unit (ICU) admission, ICU length of stay, hospital length of stay, and in-hospital mortality.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI)
title: Dexmedetomidine vs Propofol Sedation in Endovascular Aortic Repair

brief_summary:
This randomized, double-blind clinical trial will compare the effects of remifentanil alone and remifentanil combined with intravenous lidocaine on the quality of tracheal extubation in adult patients undergoing elective thyroidectomy under general anesthesia.

A total of 60 patients will be randomly assigned to two groups. Both groups will receive remifentanil during emergence from anesthesia, while one group will additionally receive intravenous lidocaine before extubation.

The primary outcome will be the incidence of coughing during tracheal extubation. Secondary outcomes will include cough severity, hemodynamic responses, oxygen saturation, airway-related adverse events, postoperative sore throat, hoarseness, postoperative nausea and vomiting, sedation level, and recovery and extubation times.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Cough During Tracheal Extubation
title: Remifentanil Versus Remifentanil-Lidocaine for Tracheal Extubation After Thyroidectomy

brief_summary:
Oral cancer, the most prevalent form of head and neck malignancy, represents a major global health burden, with over 370,000 new cases annually according to the World Health Organization. Surgical resection with free flap reconstruction remains the gold standard for curative treatment, yet it often entails significant functional and physical impairment. The surgical procedure often involves tumor resection and reconstruction. Postoperative complications such as dysphagia, reduced masticatory function, and prolonged immobility frequently contribute to fatigue, loss of muscle mass, and delayed recovery, ultimately impacting quality of life and overall prognosis.

Loss of skeletal muscle mass, commonly observed in this patient population, is strongly associated with impaired physical performance, reduced treatment tolerance, and increased postoperative morbidity. Recent evidence underscores that early mobilization and structured physiotherapeutic interventions can mitigate these effects, enhance functional recovery, and reduce length of hospital stay across various surgical populations. In head and neck cancer specifically, early mobilization has been associated with shorter hospitalization and fewer complications, yet practical, standardized physiotherapy protocols remain scarce and poorly defined.

Despite inclusion of early mobilization principles in Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways, current head and neck cancer guidelines lack specific recommendations regarding the timing, intensity, and content of postoperative physical activity. Furthermore, evidence on patient compliance and feasibility of such interventions during the acute hospitalization phase is limited.
interventions: Tailored physiotherapy program for early mobilization after oral cancer surgery
primary_outcomes: Achievement of the highest exercise progression level
title: Rehabilitation Through Individualized Support and Exercise
Examining a New Insomnia Treatment for People Living With Secondary Breast Cancer.

brief_summary:
The purpose of this non-interventional, observational, real-world study is to find out what are the real-world experiences of people living with hemophilia A or B\[OK1.1\] who start the study medicine (called marstacimab) in routine clinical practice. Hemophilia is a rare genetic condition where the blood does not clot normally, meaning people bleed longer than usual after an injury.

This study is seeking participants who are living with hemophilia A or B and:

* Have a medical record documenting hemophilia A or hemophilia B. A hematologist must have confirmed the diagnosis before they join the study.
* Are under current treatment with marstacimab or have a prescription to start the treatment with marstacimab
* Are 6 years of age or older and the recipient of medical care in the United States All participants in this study will receive their usual treatment for hemophilia A or hemophilia B Participants will take part in this study for 1 year. During this time, they will complete up to six surveys. These surveys will be given between enrollment and about one year after marstacimab is started.

Some participants in the study may be asked to take part in interviews. During these interviews they will be asked about their experience with hemophilia or marstacimab.

The study will provide information about how well the marstacimab treatment works. It will also assess treatment burden, and treatment preferences. This information will help to determine its benefit compared to existing treatment options. It will also help doctors make treatment decisions and optimize hemophilia care.
primary_outcomes: Patient reported responses to Marstacimab Patient Preference Survey (MPPS)
title: A Study to Learn About the Study Medicine (Called Marstacimab) in People With Hemophilia A or B

brief_summary:
Dental anxiety is common in children and may interfere with cooperation during dental treatment. Audiovisual distraction using virtual reality glasses may help redirect attention away from dental stimuli and improve the patient experience.

This completed prospective non-randomized controlled clinical study evaluated the effect of virtual reality audiovisual distraction on anxiety-related variables in pediatric patients undergoing dental treatment at the Dental Clinic of Universidad Europea de Madrid. Participants received either standard dental care without audiovisual distraction or standard dental care while using virtual reality glasses during the procedure.

Dental anxiety was assessed using the Modified Facial Image Scale. Heart rate and peripheral oxygen saturation were recorded using pediatric pulse oximetry. Behavioral response was assessed using the FLACC scale. Measurements were taken before, during, and after dental treatment; in the virtual reality group, additional measurements were collected while the child was using the glasses and after the glasses were removed. This record was submitted after completion of participant enrollment and data collection for retrospective public registration.
interventions: Audiovisual distraction using virtual reality glasses
primary_outcomes: Change in dental anxiety assessed using the Modified Facial Image Scale
title: Virtual Reality Audiovisual Distraction During Pediatric Dental Treatment

brief_summary: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a widespread pathology affecting over 200 million adults globally and is primarily caused by atherosclerosis. It leads to peripheral arterial stenosis, commonly in the lower extremities, resulting in symptoms ranging from intermittent claudication to chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). Endovascular interventions are currently considered first-line treatment approaches for PAD. Laser atherectomy offers a minimally invasive endovascular option to effectively debulk atherosclerotic steno-occlusive lesions prior to balloon angioplasty, minimizing vessel dissection and the need for stenting. Additionally, recent multicenter randomized controlled trials have demonstrated that sirolimus-coated balloon (SCB) angioplasty is a safe and effective treatment method for PAD. Although safety and efficacy of both laser atherectomy and SCBs are recognized, their combination for the treatment of patients with CLTI has not been adequately investigated. This research pilot study aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of combined laser atherectomy and SCB angioplasty for the treatment of CLTI. Key endpoints of the study include technical success rate, major adverse events, rates of limb salvage and target lesion reintervention, clinical improvement and overall patient survival rate.
interventions: Laser atherectomy followed by Sirolimus-coated balloon angioplasty of femoropopliteal or infrapopliteal or both arterial stenosis or occlusions
title: Laser Atherectomy and Sirolimus-coated Balloon Angioplasty for CLTI

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if the way wheat flour is ground - by stone milling (an older method) or roller milling (used for most flour today) - changes blood sugar levels after eating bread, in healthy adults aged 20 to 40 who eat bread regularly. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does bread made from stone-milled flour cause a smaller rise in blood sugar after breakfast than bread made from roller-milled flour? Does the milling method change stomach symptoms such as bloating?

Researchers will compare bread made from stone-milled wheat flour to bread made from roller-milled wheat flour, made from the same wheat and prepared the same way, to see if milling method changes blood sugar and stomach symptoms.

Participants will:

Eat the study bread at breakfast and lunch for 3 days, then switch to the other bread for 3 days, in a random order Eat a standard bread for a few days before each 3-day period Wear a small sensor that tracks blood sugar day and night for 14 days Keep a daily food diary, including photos of meals Answer online questionnaires about stomach symptoms
primary_outcomes: Incremental Area Under the Curve (iAUC) for postprandial glucose response to breakfast
title: Effects of Wheat Flour Milling Method on Glycemic Response and Gastrointestinal Symptoms

brief_summary: This phase IV trial compares how well methadone plus standard fentanyl given during surgery (intraoperative) works compared to intraoperative standard fentanyl alone in managing pain after surgery (postoperative) among patients with head and neck cancers. For most head and neck cancers, the standard treatment is surgery to remove the cancer followed by surgical reconstruction, which often requires tissue harvested from another part of the body-known as a "free flap tissue transfer". These procedures are highly complex, demand a two-surgeon team, and often take many hours to complete. The combination of multiple operative sites and extent of the surgery contributes to significant postoperative pain. Methadone is not yet used in the head and neck population but has been utilized in other subspecialties like spine and cardiac surgery. The benefits of methadone may include improved pain control in the first 72 hours postoperatively requiring less opioids postoperatively and improvement in overall pain scores. Giving intraoperative methadone plus standard fentanyl may work better than fentanyl alone in managing postoperative pain among patients with head and neck cancers.
primary_outcomes: Total morphine milligram equivalents (MMEs) administered in the first 24 hours postoperatively
title: Intraoperative Methadone for the Management of Postoperative Pain in Patients With Head and Neck Cancers

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if the DETECTRA remote monitoring platform can help clinicians detect rheumatoid arthritis (RA) disease flares earlier and more reliably, as well as identify response and non-response or insufficient response to treatment, compared with standard care. The study will include patients with RA and will follow them for 12 months.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

In patients with remission or low disease activity (DAS28-CRP ≤ 2.6), does remote monitoring with patient-reported outcomes and self-performed imaging using DETECTRA enable earlier detection of disease flares compared with standard care? In patients with higher disease activity (DAS28-CRP \> 2.6) who have switched medication, does DETECTRA enable earlier and more reliable identification of response and non-response or insufficient response to treatment compared with standard care?

Researchers will compare the DETECTRA intervention groups with standard-of-care control groups to see whether remote monitoring enables earlier and more reliable detection of changes in disease activity and treatment response.

Participants will:

Be assigned to a Low Disease Activity (LDA) or High Disease Activity (HDA) substudy based on their DAS28-CRP score at baseline.

Be randomly assigned within their substudy to either the DETECTRA remote monitoring group or the standard-of-care group.

In the DETECTRA group, regularly provide patient-reported outcomes and perform self-imaging of their hands remotely using the DETECTRA application.

Attend standard clinical assessments and be followed for 12 months.
primary_outcomes: Time to response to treatment detection
title: DETECTRA: Remote Monitoring to Detect Rheumatoid Arthritis Flares and Treatment Response

brief_summary:
Before kidney stone surgery with a flexible or semirigid ureteroscope, patients must read and sign a written consent form, but many patients find these forms long and hard to understand. This study tests whether listening to an audio recording of the same consent form, in addition to the usual written form and the surgeon's explanation, helps patients understand the operation better. It also asks whether it matters if the recording is read by a real urologist or produced by artificial intelligence (AI) from a clone of that same urologist's voice.

Adults scheduled for their first ureteroscopy or retrograde intrarenal surgery at three hospitals in Türkiye will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: (A) standard written consent only, (B) standard consent plus an audio recording read by a urologist, or (C) standard consent plus the same text produced by an AI-cloned version of the same urologist's voice. All three groups receive exactly the same information, word for word; only the way it is delivered differs. Patients in group C are told that the voice was produced by AI.

The main outcome is a 10-question knowledge test on the content of the consent form, taken immediately after the consent process. Anxiety (State-Trait Anxiety Inventory) and satisfaction are also measured on the same day. No forms are completed on the day of surgery.
title: Human Voice vs AI-Cloned Voice Audio Added to Written Consent Before Ureteroscopy or Retrograde Intrarenal Surgery (AUDIO-CONSENT)

brief_summary:
This Phase 3 study will be conducted in different countries around the world with up to approximately 602 participants.

The purpose of this study is to evaluate how well Rina-S alone or in combination with an approved, standard of care (SOC) treatment works against ovarian cancer (including primary peritoneal or fallopian tube cancer) compared to the same available SOC therapy by itself, or no treatment (only monitoring).

On average, the expected trial duration for an individual participant will be approximately 4 years (depending on treatment received). The treatment length and follow-up duration will be different for every participant, but an average of 16 months of treatment is expected, followed by an estimated 29-month post treatment follow up period.

Participation in the study will require visits to the study site(s). Participants will be asked to attend 1 to 3 visits at the study clinic for each cycle (duration of cycle is 3 weeks). During site visits, there will be various tests (such as blood draws) and procedures (such as recording of heart activity, imaging/X-rays) to monitor whether the trial treatment is safe and effective. If a participant's cancer stays the same or gets better, and there are not any serious problems, participants can keep receiving trial treatment for the protocol-defined study duration.
primary_outcomes: Progression-free Survival (PFS), per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) Version 1.1, as Determined by Blinded Independent Central Review (BICR)
title: Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Rina-S Plus Standard of Care Compared to Standard of Care Maintenance Treatment After First-line (1L) Platinum-based Chemotherapy in Participants With Ovarian Cancer

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical research study is to find out if low-dose colchicine (an anti-inflammatory drug) lowers the rate of radiation-related side effects to the carotid artery in patients who have completed radiation therapy for head and neck cancer.
title: A Ph2, Colchicine For Inflammatory Carotid Injury And Disease Evolution After Radiotherapy

brief_summary: Pulmonary vein isolation is an established intervention for atrial fibrillation. Patients with a paroxysmal atrial fibrillation have no or only few comorbidities and a good prognosis in respect to their atrial fibrillation. In contrast, patients with persistent atrial fibrillation often suffer from relevant comorbidities and recurrence of atrial fibrillation is common. Left-atrial fibrosis and its electrophysiological consequences are involved in the recurrence rate, but pathophysiological mechanisms are yet to be better characterized. The study investigates relevant comorbidities to elucidated their effect on atrial fibrosis and recurrence rates of atrial fibrillation. Furthermore, the investigators evaluate the prevalence of these comorbidities.
primary_outcomes: quantification of area of left-atrial fibrosis in the heart
Rate of recurrence of atrial fibrillation (yes/no) in the study group
title: Left-atrial Fibrosis in Persistent Atrial Fibrillation and Its Comorbidities

brief_summary:
This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial aims to investigate the effects of supplementation with peptides derived from Vicia faba L. combined with supervised resistance training in physically active and inactive older adults.

Approximately 100 adults aged 60 years or older will be enrolled. Participants will first be classified as physically active or inactive according to their habitual physical activity level and will then be randomly assigned to receive either Vicia faba L.-derived peptides (2.5 g/day) or placebo. All participants will complete the same supervised resistance training program three times per week for four weeks and will receive nutritional monitoring.

Assessments will be performed before and after the intervention to investigate changes in muscle strength and power, body composition, functional mobility, postural balance, physical function, frailty, mental health, quality of life, and cognitive performance. The study will also examine whether habitual physical activity level influences the responses to the combined supplementation and resistance training intervention.
title: VICIA FABA PEPTIDES AND RESISTANCE TRAINING IN THE ELDERLY

brief_summary:
Every course of obesity pharmacotherapy ends. Cost, supply, pregnancy plans, side effects, or the patient's own wish. In Egypt, cost alone makes discontinuation the rule, not the exception. Yet the entire evidence base describes what happens when the drug stops, and none of it tests how to stop.

Abrupt withdrawal fails predictably. One year after stopping semaglutide, STEP 1 extension participants had regained two thirds of their lost weight. SURMOUNT-4 showed the same pattern after tirzepatide withdrawal, and meta-analysis confirms it across agents. After MBS specifically, stopping GLP-1 therapy is likewise followed by regain.

The guidelines say: do not stop at all. The 2026 ADA and Obesity Association Standards strongly recommend continuing medication through maintenance, and the 2024 IFSO consensus agrees that when medication is needed to hold the benefit after MBS, ongoing treatment is probably necessary, while stating, at 94% agreement, that intermittent therapy and dose-reduction strategies require research. Our patients cannot follow the first recommendation. Cost decides for them. This trial is the research the second sentence asks for: the evidence for the moment when continuing is not an option.

Clinicians already taper, on no evidence. A 2025 expert commentary describes 8-to-12-week dose reductions in routine practice and states plainly that the approach is anecdotal and untested (Obesity and Endocrinology 2025). Practice has run ahead of the trial.

The general-population trial now exists, and we cite it rather than duplicate it. The REST trial has registered exactly this comparison, gradual 16-week dose reduction versus abrupt cessation, in non-surgical patients with obesity. No such trial exists after MBS.
lead_sponsor: General Committee of Teaching Hospitals and Institutes, Egypt
title: Tapered Versus Abrupt Discontinuation of Semaglutide After Treatment of Recurrent Weight Gain or Suboptimal Response Following Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery

brief_summary: This is a prospective, multi-center, single-arm study to assess the safety and effectiveness of Microport CardioFlow Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement system in the treatment of moderate to severe or severe degenerative mitral regurgitation and to provide the clinical evidence for product registration in China or other countries
interventions: Microport CardioFlow Mitral Valve Replacement System
lead_sponsor: Shanghai MicroPort CardioFlow Medtech Co., Ltd.
primary_outcomes: Rate of cumulative all-cause mortality at 12 months post-procedure
title: CardioFlow Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement System Pre-market Clinical Investigation

brief_summary:
Obesity has a serious impact on people's health and quality of life. For those with advanced kidney disease (i.e. approaching the need for dialysis), obesity is especially problematic - obesity can not only lead to worsening kidney function and kidney failure, but it can also prevent patients from receiving a lifesaving kidney transplantation due to concerns about operation risks. Unfortunately, there is an urgent need but no rigorously proven treatments to help people with advanced kidney disease lose weight effectively and safely.

The investigative team is a large team of doctors, nurses, dieticians, exercise specialists, social scientists, and patients with a lived experience, have spent three years advancing research to help people with advanced kidney disease achieve a healthier body weight. They have created a special weight loss program that combines individualized coaching on diet and save activity with a medication proven to help people with healthier kidneys lose weight (i.e. Ozempic). This research program is called PIVOT: Patient-centred Intervention with Virtual support for Obesity and kidney Transplant access.

The investigators have started to test PIVOT in a small pilot study and early results show that there is potential to study the program on a much larger scale (i.e. across Canada). With funding from CIHR, the investigators aim to reach more Canadians with advanced kidney disease (including people of lower income, women, and people of different races) with an aim of helping them lose weight safely, feel better, obtain a kidney transplant, and staying healthier over the longer term.
title: Patient-centred Intervention With Virtual Support for Obesity and Kidney Transplant Access

brief_summary: Shared decision-making (SDM) is the accepted ethical and legal standard for informed consent, but it is not known how it operates in anesthesia consent for cesarean delivery. Neuraxial anesthesia is recommended for most cesarean deliveries, and many anesthesiologists therefore present it as the only primary option, with general anesthesia (GA) available only as a rescue. Others present GA as a genuine alternative the patient can choose. This study will observe the existing variation in practice and will not change care. A trained observer will attend the pre-operative anesthesia consent encounter for women having an elective cesarean delivery at BC Women's Hospital and record which options were presented, using the observer-rated OPTION-5 instrument. Written research consent and a questionnaire follow 24-48 hours after delivery, and include the 9-item Shared Decision Making Questionnaire (SDM-Q-9). The primary aim is to compare patient-perceived SDM (SDM-Q-9) between consultations in which GA was offered as a genuine primary option and those in which it was not. We hypothesize that the SDM-Q-9 score will be higher when GA was offered as a primary option. Secondary aims are to describe observed SDM, decisional conflict, provider-level variation, and women's preference to be offered a choice in a future cesarean. The findings will inform a planned interventional trial of a standardized consent model.
interventions: Observation of anesthesia consent encounter and postpartum questionnaire
title: Shared Decision-Making During Anesthesia Consent for Elective Cesarean Delivery

brief_summary:
This study will examine whether warming patients before colon resection surgery improves blood flow in the fingers during early recovery from general anesthesia. It will also compare two warming durations. A total of 108 adults scheduled for elective colon resection surgery at Kayseri City Hospital will be assigned by chance to one of three groups: 10 minutes of warming before anesthesia, 30 minutes of warming before anesthesia, or no active warming before anesthesia. All three groups will receive warming during surgery as part of routine care.

Warming will be provided using a forced-air warming system. After surgery, a sensor placed on a finger will measure the perfusion index, a noninvasive indicator of blood flow, on arrival in the recovery unit and 5 and 10 minutes later. The main comparison will use the average of these three measurements. The researchers will also assess other circulation measurements, routine blood gas and lactate results, shivering, pain, the time until oral feeding begins, and wound infection during the 14 days after surgery.
title: Effect of Prewarming Duration on Blood Flow After Colon Resection Surgery

brief_summary: This educational intervention study evaluates evidence-based practice (EBP) education among social work students. The study will assess changes in students' engagement with the EBP process, attitudes toward evidence-based interventions, information literacy, and perceived social work competence following the educational intervention.
primary_outcomes: Change in Evidence-Based Practice Process Assessment Scale (EBPPAS) score
title: Evidence-Based Practice in Social Work Education

brief_summary: This cross-sectional study aims to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of chest ultrasound in the diagnosis of respiratory distress syndrome among preterm neonates in comparison with chest X-ray.
primary_outcomes: Sensitivity of chest ultrasound for diagnosis of respiratory distress syndrome
title: Chest Ultrasound Versus Chest X-ray in Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome

brief_summary: The objective of the study is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of SI-B036 in participants with solid tumors who have received at least one prior line of therapy for advanced disease.
primary_outcomes: Participants with Serious Adverse Events (SAEs), Adverse Events of Special Interest (AESIs), and Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs)
Participants with abnormal physical examination findings
To determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) if reached or minimum safe and pharmacologically effective dose (MSED).
title: SI-B036-ST-101 in Advanced/Metastatic Solid Tumors

brief_summary:
Serious infections caused by gram-positive bacteria often require several weeks of antibiotic treatment, which may involve prolonged hospitalisation, intravenous treatment and long-term vascular access. Dalbavancin is a long-acting antibiotic that can be given less frequently than conventional intravenous antibiotics.

EDGAR is a multicentre prospective observational study involving up to 50 adults receiving dalbavancin as part of routine clinical care for serious gram-positive infections. The decision to prescribe dalbavancin, including dose, timing and duration, is made by the treating clinician independently of participation in EDGAR.

EDGAR will collect scheduled pharmacokinetic and therapeutic drug monitoring (PK/TDM) blood samples and clinical, safety and participant-reported outcome data. PK modelling and Bayesian forecasting will be undertaken retrospectively and will not be used to guide treatment during EDGAR. Participants will be followed to Day 180.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants Completing Protocol-Specified Pharmacokinetic Sampling Associated With Clinically Administered Dalbavancin Doses
Proportion of Participants With Pharmacokinetically Evaluable Data for External Model Validation
title: Optimised Dalbavancin Dosing for Serious Gram-Positive Bacterial Infections

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled clinical trial is to evaluate whether a brief preoperative video-guided breathing exercise reduces postoperative pain in adults undergoing single-visit root canal treatment for symptomatic irreversible pulpitis.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does a 2-minute video-guided breathing exercise reduce postoperative pain 24 hours after root canal treatment compared with a 2-minute period of passive rest?
* Does the breathing exercise affect pain experienced during root canal treatment or postoperative pain at 6, 12, 48, and 72 hours?
* Does the breathing exercise reduce the need for supplemental local anesthesia during treatment?
* Does the breathing exercise reduce analgesic use during the first 72 hours after treatment?
* Does the breathing exercise produce a greater immediate change in heart rate compared with passive rest?

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups before root canal treatment.

In the video-guided breathing exercise group, participants will watch a standardized 2-minute video and follow a controlled breathing pattern consisting of inhaling through the nose for 4 seconds followed by exhaling for 6 seconds. This breathing cycle will be repeated throughout the video.

In the passive rest group, participants will remain seated in the dental chair for 2 minutes without receiving any breathing or relaxation instructions and will be asked to breathe normally.

All participants will then receive single-visit root canal treatment using the same standardized endodontic treatment protocol.

Postoperative pain will be assessed at 6, 12, 24, 48, and 72 hours after treatment. Pain at 24 hours will be the primary outcome. Maximum pain experienced during treatment, supplemental anesthesia requirement, analgesic use during the first 72 hours, and change in heart rate immediately before and after the assigned preoperative intervention will also be evaluated.
title: Preoperative Video-Guided Breathing Exercise for Pain After Root Canal Treatment

brief_summary:
Invasive blood pressure monitoring is essential during heart surgery. Usually, doctors measure blood pressure using a small tube (a catheter) placed in an artery, typically in the wrist or arm. During surgeries that require a heart-lung machine (cardiopulmonary bypass), doctors can also measure blood pressure directly near the heart in the main artery (the aorta). This is done using a tube already in place for the machine, so no extra procedure is needed.

In adult patients, doctors have noticed that blood pressure readings taken at the arm can sometimes be significantly different from readings taken near the heart right after coming off the heart-lung machine. This difference could lead to unnecessary or incorrect treatments if medical teams rely only on arm readings. However, it is still unknown whether this same difference occurs in children.

The goal of this study is to measure and compare blood pressure from both the arm and near the heart in children aged 3 years and younger as they come off the heart-lung machine during heart surgery. This research will help medical teams make safer, more accurate treatment decisions for children undergoing heart surgery.

brief_summary:
Purpose Hip fractures in older adults often cause a serious loss of strength and independence. Physical therapy helps people recover, but patients do not always exercise consistently or correctly. This study tests whether adding an automated motivational support tool to physical therapy helps patients recover better than physical therapy alone.

How the tool works The tool uses a regular camera to record movement during exercise. It does not use facial recognition. It gives the patient simple, encouraging messages, such as "great job" or "keep going." It does not give medical advice or correct the patient's movements during the session. The research team reviews the recordings later; they are not reviewed in real time.

Who can join People age 70 or older who had surgery for a hip fracture and are staying in the Orthogeriatrics Unit at Ramón y Cajal University Hospital, in Madrid, Spain.

What happens in the study Forty-eight people will take part.

Half will receive standard physical therapy plus one daily session with the motivational tool.

Half will receive standard physical therapy alone.

Researchers will measure physical performance with a short walking and balance test. They will measure it three times: at the start, when the patient leaves the hospital, and one month later.

Why it matters This study will show whether an automated motivational tool helps patients recover more strength and function after a hip fracture.

This study will investigate the effects of a Leap Motion-based virtual reality intervention on fine motor skills and daily living performance in children aged 5-10 years with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Children with ASD may experience difficulties in motor coordination, hand use, attention, and daily activities, which may affect their participation in everyday life.

The study will include children with ASD who attend occupational therapy sessions and meet the study eligibility criteria. Participants will receive a structured virtual reality-based intervention using Leap Motion technology. The intervention will provide controlled, repetitive, and task-oriented activities involving hand and finger movements.

Fine motor skills, daily living performance, and cognitive functioning will be assessed before and after the intervention using standardized assessment tools, including the Nine Hole Peg Test, the Canadian Occupational Performance Measure, and the Mini-Mental State Examination. Changes in fine motor performance and daily living performance from before to after the intervention will be examined.

The study aims to determine whether a Leap Motion-based virtual reality intervention may support fine motor skills and functional performance in children with ASD.

brief_summary:
Periodontitis is a chronic multifactorial inflammatory disorder affecting the periodontium, often implicated with microbial dysbiosis. Following the establishment of a proper diagnosis, the initial therapeutic phase within the recommended protocol must focus patient motivation and behavior alongside the comprehensive management of modifiable local and systemic risk factors (1). Although SRP effectively reduces microbial load, complete regeneration of periodontal tissues remains challenging due to limited healing potential and persistent inflammation. Various adjunctive therapies have been explored to enhance periodontal healing, including oxygen-based and platelet concentrate approaches (2).

Topical oxygen therapy has recently gained attention for its antimicrobial and regenerative properties. Oxygen-releasing gels, such as those containing stabilized hydrogen peroxide, increase local oxygen tension, inhibit anaerobic pathogens, and promote angiogenesis and fibroblast proliferation, resulting in improved clinical parameters following SRP (3).

Injectable platelet-rich fibrin (i-PRF), a second-generation autologous platelet concentrate, provides a sustained release of growth factors such as PDGF, VEGF, and TGF-β, enhancing soft tissue healing and bone regeneration. Clinical trials have demonstrated that i-PRF used with SRP significantly improves probing depth reduction, attachment gain, and bleeding scores compared with SRP alone. However, no studies have directly compared oxygen therapy and i-PRF as adjuncts to non-surgical periodontal therapy. Investigating these two bio stimulatory approaches could identify a minimally invasive, cost-effective strategy to optimize periodontal healing and regeneration.
title: Injectable Platelet-Rich Fibrin (i-PRF) and Oxygen-Releasing Gel in the Treatment of Stage II Periodontitis.

Participants will provide informed consent and have a routine blood draw. The study does not assign treatment or require additional diagnostic procedures, and all medical decisions remain with the treating clinician. brief_summary:
This prospective, controlled observational study aims to evaluate three-dimensional (3D) facial soft tissue changes following miniscrew-assisted rapid palatal expansion (MARPE) and determine whether these changes are clinically perceptible to orthodontic specialists and patients.

A total of 55 postpubertal participants aged 16-25 years will be included: 40 patients undergoing MARPE as part of their routine orthodontic treatment and 15 control participants who will not undergo maxillary expansion. Treatment decisions will be made independently of study participation.

Facial soft tissue changes will be assessed using 3D facial scans. The MARPE group will be scanned before expansion (T0), immediately after active expansion (T1), and three months after expansion (T2). The control group will undergo two facial scans at comparable baseline and follow-up intervals.

Changes in facial regions, including the nose, paranasal area, midface, and upper lip, will be evaluated. Blinded orthodontic specialists will assess the clinical perceptibility of changes using standardized facial images, while participants will provide their own perception of facial changes through questionnaires. When available from routine clinical records, skeletal and dental expansion measurements will also be analyzed in relation to the observed soft tissue changes.

The study aims to clarify the magnitude, distribution, and clinical relevance of facial soft tissue changes associated with MARPE.

title: Three-Dimensional Facial Soft Tissue Changes and Clinical Perception Following MARPE

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to characterize regional intestinal fermentation physiology and determine how the response to fermentable dietary fiber differs between healthy individuals and individuals with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). The study will use ingestible capsule technologies to directly measure intestinal gases and regional microbiome composition following low-fiber and high-fiber meal challenges.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does the change in regional intestinal gas levels following a fermentable-fiber challenge differ between participants with IBS and healthy controls? How are regional intestinal gas dynamics associated with microbiome composition, breath gases, serum short-chain fatty acids, glucose dynamics, metabolites, and gastrointestinal symptoms?

Researchers will compare participants with IBS to healthy controls to determine whether intestinal fermentation responses to dietary fiber differ between these populations.

Participants will:

Complete two study visits approximately one week apart. At one visit, participants will receive a low-fiber control meal, and at the other visit, they will receive the same base meal containing 15 g of inulin. The order of the two meals will be assigned at random.

Swallow an Atmo gas-sensing capsule to measure intestinal H2, CO2, and O2 and a CapScan capsule to collect regional intestinal fluid for microbiome analysis.

Undergo serial blood and breath sampling and gastrointestinal symptom assessments during each 8-hour study visit.

Complete stool and urine collections, dietary assessment, and continuous glucose monitoring before and/or after the study visits.
primary_outcomes: Successful Acquisition of a Complete Regional Multiomic Fermentation-Physiology Dataset
title: High-Resolution Measurements of Diet-Microbiome Interactions

There is an unmet medical need to treat people with advanced cancer in the stomach, or where the food pipe joins the stomach. These conditions are known as advanced gastric cancer or advanced gastroesophageal cancer (GEJ for short).

Some people with stomach or GEJ cancer have a protein called Claudin 18.2 in their tumor. Zolbetuximab works by attaching to the Claudin 18.2 protein in their tumor. This switches on the body's immune system to attack the tumor.

The main aim of the study is to collect information about zolbetuximab and other cancer treatments in people with advanced gastric or GEJ cancer. This includes safety information, how long people respond to treatment and how long people live for without their cancer getting worse.

This study is about collecting information only. This is known as an observational study. The individual's doctor decides on treatment, not the sponsor (Astellas).

This study will use information from European and Canadian health registries and databases to learn more about people with advanced gastric or GEJ cancers who used zolbetuximab and other cancer treatments. The entire study will last about 4 years.

brief_summary: This is a prospective, multicenter, open-label, non-inferiority, randomized controlled trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of very low plasma exchange (400 mL plasma + prothrombin complex concentrate) and plasma-free (prothrombin complex concentrate only) artificial liver support systems compared with standard low-volume plasma exchange (1000 mL plasma) in patients with acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF). A total of 840 eligible patients (COSSH grade 1-2) will be enrolled from 10 centers across China and randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive three sessions of treatment (every 2-3 days) combined with standard medical therapy. The primary endpoint is 28-day non-liver-transplant mortality, with a non-inferiority margin of 10%. Secondary endpoints include 90-day non-liver-transplant mortality, 90-day bridging to liver transplantation rate, changes in prognostic scores (COSSH-ACLF Ⅱ, MELD, CLIF-C ACLFs) from baseline at 2 weeks, and total plasma volume used during hospitalization. Safety outcomes include adverse events (bleeding, coagulation disorders, thrombosis, hypotension, infections, allergic reactions). The study aims to establish a plasma-sparing treatment strategy that reduces dependence on blood products while maintaining non-inferior efficacy. The trial is funded by the National Science and Technology Major Project of China and approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of the Third Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University (Approval No.: 中大附三医伦RG2026-044-01; Approval Date: April 29, 2026). Enrollment is planned from May 2026 to October 2027, with follow-up completed by October 2028. Written informed consent will be obtained from all participants.

title: Very Low-volume Plasma Exchange in ACLF

It also seeks to assess differences in treatment response among PD subtypes (tremor-dominant, rigidity-dominant, and mixed) and across disease stages (early stage, Hoehn and Yahr \[H\&Y\] stages 1-2, and mid-to-late stage, H\&Y stages 2.5-3). The study will enroll eligible PD patients and evaluate their condition using the Movement Disorder Society-Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (MDS-UPDRS), the 39-item Parkinson's Disease Questionnaire (PDQ-39), the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA), the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD), and a visual analog scale (VAS) for fatigue. Assessments will be performed before routine tTIS treatment, immediately after treatment, and at two and four weeks post-treatment, in order to analyze the therapeutic effect of tTIS in PD. This is an observational study without any intervention; all enrolled participants will receive standard medical care and health education.

brief_summary:
Black women are more likely than White women to be diagnosed at later stages and to die from breast cancer. Increasing breast cancer screening rates could help improve early detection of and survival from breast cancer. To this end, this study seeks to implement and evaluate a culturally tailored chatbot intervention to increase breast cancer screening and address inequities among Black women using community-based research approaches.

We will conduct a pilot randomized quality improvement trial to test the efficacy of a chatbot outreach intervention, which provides breast cancer screening education and direct links to scheduling, on increasing breast cancer screening completion among Black women who receive primary care at the University of Washington (UW) Medicine. We hypothesize that compared to women who receive usual care, women who receive this novel chatbot outreach will have higher breast cancer screening completion rates at 90-days. In addition to quantitative assessment of chatbot effectiveness, we will also qualitatively evaluate chatbot acceptability, feasibility, and message relevance through interviews with a small group of participants about their experiences with the chatbot.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants completing BCS 90 days after initial outreach

The study is intended to provide a culturally adapted, valid, and reliable Turkish version of the r-B-CRPS-BPDS for assessing body perception disturbance in individuals with CRPS.

brief_summary:
Sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a serious condition where severe infection causes fluid accumulation in the lungs, often requiring invasive mechanical ventilation. Patients with low blood albumin levels are particularly vulnerable to this fluid leakage, leading to prolonged dependence on a ventilator.

This observational study evaluates the association between a targeted human albumin treatment strategy combined with clinically guided fluid removal, and clinical outcomes in adults with sepsis-associated ARDS and low blood albumin levels (≤ 30 g/L).

Conducted at a single hospital, this study compares two groups. The prospective group consists of patients receiving current usual clinical care, where albumin administration and fluid management are determined by the treating clinical team. Their outcomes will be compared to a historical control group of similar patients who received standard care before this targeted albumin management strategy was routinely implemented.

The primary objective is to evaluate whether this targeted albumin strategy is associated with an increase in Ventilator-Free Days at day 28 (VFD-28). VFD-28 reflects both patient survival and successful liberation from the ventilator. The study will also observe secondary outcomes including oxygenation improvement, fluid balance, organ function, mortality, and safety events (e.g., fluid overload or allergic reactions). As an observational study, researchers do not assign treatments; all interventions are based on real-world clinical judgment.
lead_sponsor: The Second Affiliated Hospital of Hainan Medical University
primary_outcomes: Cumulative Incidence of Successful Liberation from Ventilation
title: Effect of Albumin Therapy in Mechanically Ventilated Patients With Sepsis-Associated ARDS

brief_summary: This prospective observational cohort study evaluated the effects of the timing of amoxicillin use on postoperative recovery and oral health-related quality of life following impacted mandibular third molar surgery. A total of 52 healthy adults aged 18-50 years were included. Participants were classified into two cohorts according to the amoxicillin regimen selected by the treating clinician based on clinical assessment: preoperative amoxicillin, initiated 3 days before surgery and continued for a total of 5 days, or postoperative amoxicillin, initiated on the day of surgery and continued for 5 days. In both cohorts, amoxicillin was administered at a dose of 1000 mg twice daily. Postoperative pain, facial swelling, maximum mouth opening, and oral health-related quality of life were assessed. Pain, swelling, and mouth opening were evaluated on postoperative days 1, 3, and 7, and quality of life was assessed using the Oral Health Impact Profile-14 (OHIP-14) on postoperative day 7. The study aimed to compare postoperative recovery between the two antibiotic-timing approaches.

brief_summary: We aim to build on our pilot study data looking at the feasibility of implementation of Goal Setting alongside Hoosier Sport at two schools (Eastern Greene Middle School and White River Valley Middle School). We plan to assess the effect of goal setting on physical activity engagement and psychological measures across the two schools. One school will receive the goal setting intervention in Fall while the other will receive it in Spring.
title: Feasibility of an Implementation Strategy for a Physical Activity Program in Rural Middle Schools

brief_summary:
This prospective, controlled, observational study aims to investigate the relationship between phoenixin (PNX) levels and pain in pediatric burn patients. A total of 87 prepubertal children under 18 years of age will be included and evaluated in three independent groups: 29 children with second-degree burns in the acute burn period and experiencing pain at the time of assessment, 29 children with a history of burn injury at least three months previously who have completed the acute burn and procedural pain period, and 29 age-similar healthy controls without a history of burns or acute pain.

Blood and urine samples will be collected from all participants, and PNX levels will be measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Pain intensity will be assessed using age-appropriate validated pain assessment tools, including the Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability (FLACC) scale and the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), as appropriate. In the burn groups, burn characteristics, including total body surface area (TBSA), will also be recorded.

The study will compare blood and urine PNX levels among the acute burn, chronic burn, and healthy control groups and will evaluate the relationship between PNX levels and clinical pain intensity in children with acute burns. Secondary analyses will examine the relationships between blood and urine PNX levels and their associations with TBSA and demographic and clinical characteristics. The findings are expected to provide preliminary clinical data on the potential role of PNX as a pain-related biological marker in pediatric burn patients.
primary_outcomes: Difference in Blood and Urine Phoenixin Levels Among the Study Groups
Association Between Phoenixin Levels and Pain Intensity in the Acute Burn Group
title: Phoenixin and Pain in Pediatric Burn Patients

brief_summary: The aim of this randomized study is to compare a live, trained simulated patient with a high-fidelity manikin in obstetric emergency team training using two standardized scenarios. The participants in this study are intact clinical teams (e.g., obstetrics, anesthesiology, and nursing/midwifery staff routinely working together in obstetric emergencies) and are recruited as a unit. Each team will either have both scenarios with the live, trained standard patient or the high fidelity manikin. Both scenarios are standardized: One scenario is about post-partum hemorrhage (PPH), a severe bleeding after giving birth, and the other scenario is about eclampsia, an emergency in obstetrics that causes hypertensive crisis and seizures. The order of scenarios is random. After each scenario all team members fill out questionnaires about realism and cognitive stress. After the second debriefing, a focus group of approximately 15 minutes is conducted with each team with a standardized procedure and questions.
title: Comparing Simulated Patients and Manikin Based Simulation in Obstetrics

brief_summary:
Pleural infection (which is the infection in the space around the lungs called the pleura) is a severe infection that is difficult to treat and can lead substantial disability or even death. This infection is associated with fluid build up in the pleura and draining this fluid is crucial in treating the infection. The typical method for draining this fluid is inserting a tube in the chest cavity. However, this is not successful in more than one third of patients and additional treatments including surgery are required. These additional treatments are expensive and hence not available in a lot of settings. In addition, patients with this type of infection are often not fit to undergo surgery.

There are studies to suggest that a minor surgical procedure, called medical thoracoscopy, that is carried out by chest doctors and does not require general anaesthesia can help with draining the fluid in the pleura when there is infection. In order to ascertain this benefit, a study is needed to compare the effect of using medical thoracoscopy to not using medical thoracoscopy in treating pleural infection. The choice of patients needs to be in random to ensure the effects are true.

The investigators aim in this study to conduct a randomized study in patients with pleural infection where half the patients will receive the standard chest tube treatment and the other half will have medical thoracoscopy in addition to the standard tube. The study will monitor the treatment outcomes for each group to find out whether the newer treatment improves these outcomes.
interventions: Medical thoracoscopy plus standard of care
title: Study of Medical Thoracoscopy in Early Pleural Infection

brief_summary: In the field of Osteopathic Medicine, diagnosis of potential areas of dysfunction are diagnosed by the physician using their hands and expertise in noticing subtle differences in symmetry, tone, swelling etc.. In this study, we propose the use of ultrasound, which is a non invasive imaging technique that requires no radiation exposure, to confirm the diagnosis made with the physician's hands. We believe this will add a layer of objectivity to this diagnosis, in that you have numbers that have been measured to back up the diagnosis made based on feel. In this study, we can confirm whether or not these differences felt are true from an objective standpoint. We will compare patients with dysfunction palpated on manual exam to those with no palpated dysfunction in terms of their median asymmetry when measured using musculoskeletal ultrasound.
lead_sponsor: The Touro College and University System
title: Use of Ultrasound Imaging in Confirming Osteopathic Spinal Diagnosis

brief_summary: Advanced PeriodontitisIn this cross-sectional study, the relationship between periodontal disease severity and retinal and choroidal structural changes was evaluated using SD-OCT. Data from a total of 80 participants were examined. It was found that choroidal thickness increased and ganglion cell layer thickness decreased as periodontal disease severity increased, while no significant relationship was found in RNFL and IPL thicknesses. The findings support a possible association between periodontal disease and ocular structural changes.
primary_outcomes: Correlation Between Periodontal Disease Severity and Choroidal Thickness
title: Retinal and Choroidal Changes in Periodontal Disease

brief_summary: This pilot randomized controlled trial will evaluate whether catheter size affects the efficacy and performance of ultra-low-flow extracorporeal carbon dioxide removal (ECCO₂R) in mechanically ventilated adults with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and hypercapnic respiratory acidosis. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive ECCO₂R using a 12F, 13F, or 15F catheter. The primary outcome is the percentage change in PaCO₂ from baseline during ECCO₂R. Secondary outcomes include achievement and time to correction of hypercapnic respiratory acidosis, changes in PaO₂, circuit lifespan, maximum blood flow, and device- and patient-related complications.
primary_outcomes: Percentage Change in PaCO₂ From Baseline
title: The Effect of Catheter Size on the Efficacy of Ultralow-flow Extracorporeal Carbon Dioxide Removal System in Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
