brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) can help prevent osteoradionecrosis (ORN) after dental extractions in adults who previously received radiation therapy to the head and neck. ORN is a condition in which jawbone damaged by radiation does not heal properly and may become exposed.

The main question this study aims to answer is:

Does placing PRF into dental extraction sites lower the chance of developing ORN within 6 months after extraction?

PRF is made from a small sample of a participant's own blood. The blood is processed in a centrifuge to form PRF, which can then be placed into the tooth extraction site.

Researchers will compare participants who receive PRF in addition to standard extraction care with participants who receive standard extraction care alone.

Participants will:

Have one or more teeth removed from an area of the jaw that previously received radiation therapy.

Be randomly assigned to receive either PRF plus standard care or standard care alone.

Return for follow-up visits at approximately 2 weeks, 6 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months after extraction.

Have their healing, pain, any potential postoperative complications, and development of ORN assessed during follow-up.
title: Platelet-Rich Fibrin for Preventing Osteoradionecrosis After Dental Extractions

brief_summary:
Pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) is commonly used in the conservative management of urinary incontinence. The aim of the study is to investigate changes in urinary incontinence symptoms and pelvic floor muscle function during a treatment program involving pelvic floor muscle exercises and the use of a dietary supplement.

The study includes women suffering from stress, urge, or mixed urinary incontinence. Participants undergo a baseline assessment followed by follow-up visits after 4 weeks and 12 weeks.

At the baseline visit, demographic and medical information is collected, including age, chronic diseases, regularly used medications, height, weight, pregnancy and delivery history, menopausal status, and previous surgical procedures.

Urinary incontinence symptoms are assessed using the Medical, Epidemiologic and Social Aspects of Aging (MESA) questionnaire. Participants also complete the Patient Global Impression of Severity (PGI-S), the Incontinence Impact Questionnaire short form (IIQ-7), the Urinary Distress Inventory short form (UDI-6), and the SF-12 Health Survey.

Pelvic floor and pelvic organ status are evaluated using Vaginal Tactile Imaging (VTI), the Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification (POP-Q) system, perineometer measurements, and manual assessment of pelvic floor muscle strength using the Oxford scale. Three perineometer measurements are recorded.

Participants receive the dietary supplement as well as a urinary diary and instructions and a diary for pelvic floor muscle exercises.

At the second visit, performed after 4 weeks, participants complete the Patient Global Impression of Improvement (PGI-I), IIQ-7, and UDI-6 questionnaires to assess changes in symptoms and their impact on daily activities and quality of life.

The third visit is performed after 12 weeks. Participants again complete the PGI-I, IIQ-7, and UDI-6 questionnaires. Pelvic floor and pelvic organ assessments are repeated, including Vaginal Tactile Imaging, POP-Q assessment, three perineometer measurements, and manual evaluation of pelvic floor muscle strength using the Oxford scale.

Changes in urinary incontinence symptoms, quality of life, patient-reported improvement, and objective pelvic floor muscle parameters are evaluated over the 12-week study period.
title: Effect of Pelvic Floor Muscle Training Combined With Dietary Supplementation on Urinary Incontinence and Pelvic Floor Muscle Function in Women

brief_summary:
Palliative care aims to improve the quality of life of patients with life-threatening illnesses and their families through early identification, assessment, and management of physical, psychosocial, and spiritual needs. The demand for palliative care is steadily increasing due to population aging, the rising prevalence of chronic diseases, and earlier identification of palliative needs. In France, access to palliative care remains insufficient, with only about half of estimated needs currently met.

Early integration of palliative care has been shown to improve quality of life, reduce depressive symptoms, and limit aggressive interventions at the end of life, particularly in oncology, with emerging evidence supporting similar benefits in non-cancer chronic diseases. At the same time, healthcare systems face significant pressure, including limited hospital bed capacity and overcrowded emergency departments, highlighting the importance of optimizing care pathways.

This retrospective study aims to analyze the care pathways of patients admitted to the palliative care unit of Strasbourg University Hospitals from their home in 2025. It will compare direct admissions to those preceded by an emergency department visit and identify clinical, organizational, and social factors associated with direct admission. The findings are expected to inform strategies to improve access to palliative care, promote home-based management when appropriate, and reduce avoidable emergency department utilization.
primary_outcomes: Admission pathway to the palliative care unit
title: Study of the Care Pathway of Patients Admitted to the Palliative Care Unit of Strasbourg University Hospital From Their Home in 2025

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to: 1) evaluate the safety, tolerability, and recommended dose of dexbrompheniramine when combined with metronomic temozolomide for adults with recurrent high-grade glioma who have been previously treated with standard of care chemoradiation therapy and 2) determine the efficacy of the combination therapy in adults with glioblastoma who progressed during the first six cycles of adjuvant standard dose temozolomide.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* What medical problems to participants have when taking dexbrompheniramine together with temozolomide?
* What is the correct dose of dexbrompheniramine to use when evaluating the safety and efficacy of the combination therapy?
* Is the combination therapy more effective at delaying disease progression compared to temozolomide alone?

Participants will take dexbrompheniramine and temozolomide every day at night.
primary_outcomes: Safety and RP2D of Combination Therapy
title: Metronomic Temozolomide With Dexbrompheniramine for Recurrent High-Grade Glioma/Glioblastoma

brief_summary: This study will investigate how different exercise intensities affect blood levels of lactoyl-phenylalanine (Lac-Phe), a metabolite that may be involved in the regulation of appetite and energy balance, in women with obesity. Participants aged 30 to 50 years with a body mass index (BMI) of 30-34.9 kg/m² will be assigned to one of three groups: high-intensity interval training (HIIT), moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT), or a control group. The exercise programs will be performed for 12 weeks. EtikBasvuruFormu DUYGU Blood samples and clinical measurements will be collected before and after the study period. The study will evaluate changes in Lac-Phe and related biochemical markers, including lactate, phenylalanine, and CNDP2, together with selected metabolic, body composition, physical activity, and appetite-related measures. The main aim is to determine whether exercise intensity influences Lac-Phe responses and whether these changes are associated with metabolic and appetite-related outcomes in women with obesity.
title: Effects of Different Exercise Intensities on Lac-Phe Levels in Women With Obesity

brief_summary: This study aims to investigate the effects of preoperative white noise and pink noise interventions on sleep quality, anxiety, postoperative pain, nausea, and physiological parameters in patients undergoing elective total hip arthroplasty (THA) or total knee arthroplasty (TKA). A total of 165 adult patients will be randomly allocated into three equal groups: a white noise group, a pink noise group, and a control group (55 participants per group). On the evening prior to surgery (around 10:00 PM), participants in the experimental groups will listen to standardized white noise or pink noise at 45-50 dB for 30 minutes via over-ear, active noise-cancelling headphones. Participants in the control group will receive routine perioperative care without any auditory intervention. Data regarding sleep quality, anxiety levels, pain intensity, nausea, and hemodynamics (blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation) will be collected using validated scales and physiological monitoring before and after the intervention as well as in the postoperative period (at 0, 12, and 24 hours).
conditions: Postoperative Pain After Arthroscopic Knee Surgery
title: The Effect of White and Pink Noise in Patients Undergoing Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty

brief_summary:
This crossover clinical trial aims to compare the accuracy of conventional splinted open-tray implant impressions with intraoral digital scanning using a calibrated framework in completely edentulous patients rehabilitated with full-arch implant-supported prostheses. Accurate transfer of implant positions is essential for achieving a passive fit of the prosthetic framework and minimizing biological and mechanical complications.

Twenty healthy completely edentulous patients requiring full-arch implant rehabilitation will be enrolled. Each participant will undergo both conventional and digital impression techniques following implant placement, allowing direct within-subject comparison. The conventional technique consists of a verified splinted open-tray impression, while the digital technique uses an intraoral scanner in combination with a calibrated stock framework.

The accuracy of the two impression techniques will be evaluated by superimposing the resulting STL files using Geomagic Control X software. Linear deviations in the x-, y-, and z-axes, angular deviations, and global deviations will be measured and compared. The findings of this study are expected to provide clinical evidence regarding the accuracy of calibrated framework-assisted intraoral scanning compared with the conventional impression technique for full-arch implant rehabilitation.
interventions: Intraoral Digital Scanning Using a Calibrated Framework
title: Accuracy of the Calibrated Framework for Intra Oral Full Arch Scan (A Cross-over Study)

brief_summary: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and dual GLP-1/GIP agonists such as semaglutide and tirzepatide produce marked weight loss in people with obesity, with reported reductions of about 15-20%. Rapid weight loss may reduce not only fat mass but also lean body mass and skeletal muscle mass, raising concern about sarcopenia and sarcopenic obesity. Evidence in non-diabetic obese individuals is limited and inconsistent. This prospective descriptive study will assess muscle mass, muscle strength, physical performance and sarcopenia risk in non-diabetic obese adults starting GLP-1 RA therapy, at baseline and at month 3, and will examine how weight loss relates to changes in body composition.
interventions: GLP-1 receptor agonist (e.g., semaglutide, tirzepatide) - prescribed by the treating physician as standard care; the study does not assign or alter treatment.
primary_outcomes: Change in SARC-F score and proportion of participants screening positive for sarcopenia (SARC-F ≥4)
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Use and Sarcopenia in Obese Individuals Without Diabetes

The follow-up is 12 months and comprises scheduled on-site examinations by physician and study nurse, scheduled phone contacts, and registrations of new LRTI-episodes (if any). Nasopharyngeal swabs and blood will be collected at specified visits. The children will be invited to a follow-up study at school age for lung function assessments.

brief_summary: This study evaluates whether a 12-week pelvic floor rehabilitation programme improves urinary incontinence symptoms in adult women treated at Hospital Nacional Edgardo Rebagliati Martins, a public tertiary hospital in Lima, Peru. Women referred by the Urology Service attend supervised group pelvic floor muscle training with a physiotherapist, together with individual sessions with a physiatrist that may include EMG biofeedback, electrical stimulation, transcutaneous tibial nerve stimulation, myofascial techniques or bladder training. The main question is whether symptom severity, measured with the ICIQ-SF questionnaire, improves between baseline and week 12. Participants are followed for 6 months.

title: Pelvic Floor Rehabilitation Programme for Women With Urinary Incontinence in a Peruvian Public Hospital

brief_summary:
Metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) is the most effective durable treatment for severe obesity, yet a clinically meaningful proportion of patients experience recurrent weight gain after an initially successful operation. Until recently, research and care in this area were limited by the absence of standardized definitions: reported prevalence of weight recurrence ranged from under 10% to over 90% depending on the metric and threshold applied, and treatment decisions varied by provider.

In 2026, an international two-round modified Delphi study of 66 experts across surgery, obesity medicine, gastroenterology, endocrinology, dietetics, and psychology (Wills et al.) established consensus definitions. The consensus specifies: (i) percentage total weight loss (%TWL) as the preferred measurement approach (94.6% agreement); (ii) surgical non-response as \<10% TWL at 12 months (73.0%); (iii) recurrent weight gain as regain of more than 25% of lost weight from nadir (70.3%); and (iv) a change of up to 10% in percentage excess weight loss from nadir as a normal physiologic fluctuation not requiring intervention (83.8%). The consensus also endorsed 'suboptimal' as the preferred terminology for poor surgical response and reached unanimous agreement that anti-obesity medications may appropriately be prescribed by specialists in this population. These definitions supersede the heterogeneous thresholds used previously, including the \>30% regain threshold of the 2024 IFSO Delphi, and are adopted throughout this protocol. Both IFSO and ASMBS now formally support pharmacotherapy as a therapeutic option for weight recurrence after MBS.

The 2024 IFSO international consensus on obesity management medications in the context of MBS reinforces this pathway: at 92% agreement, medications should generally be considered before revisional surgery for recurrent weight gain; at 100%, medication efficacy appears broadly preserved after MBS; and at 97%, no clear increase in adverse effects after MBS has been demonstrated. RESURGE supplies the randomized evidence behind the first of these statements.
lead_sponsor: General Committee of Teaching Hospitals and Institutes, Egypt
primary_outcomes: Mean percentage change in body weight from randomization
title: Semaglutide 2.4 mg Once Weekly for Recurrent Weight Gain After Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery (RESURGE)

brief_summary: This observational study aims to investigate the associations between multidimensional human phenotypic characteristics and growth and developmental features. A total of 500 participants aged 6 to 60 years are planned to be enrolled. Multidimensional phenotypic characteristics will be assessed using non-invasive methods, including fingerprint imaging, foot morphology assessment, facial and tongue feature acquisition, anthropometric measurements, and musculoskeletal examinations. Development-related musculoskeletal characteristics, including plantar arch morphology, lower-limb alignment, joint range of motion, and generalized joint mobility, will also be assessed. The collected data will be analyzed to explore associations between external phenotypic characteristics and musculoskeletal growth and developmental features.
primary_outcomes: Foot Arch Morphology Assessed by Arch Index
Generalized Joint Hypermobility Assessed by Beighton Score
title: A Study on Associations Between Multidimensional Human Phenotypic Traits and Human Growth and Development

brief_summary:

brief_summary:
This prospective observational cohort study aims to investigate the relationship between perioperative endogenous melatonin levels and postoperative delirium in patients aged 65 years or older undergoing elective abdominal cancer surgery. The study will also evaluate serotonin, kynurenine, kynurenic acid, and vitamin B12 as potential biomarkers associated with postoperative delirium.

Participants will undergo routine standardized general anesthesia and thoracic epidural analgesia. Venous blood samples will be obtained preoperatively and on postoperative day 3. In participants who develop delirium, an additional blood sample will be obtained as soon as possible after delirium is detected. Postoperative delirium will be assessed using the Confusion Assessment Method (CAM) on postoperative days 1, 3, and 5. No experimental drug or additional therapeutic intervention will be administered as part of the study.
primary_outcomes: Change in Serum Melatonin Concentration From Preoperative Baseline to Postoperative Day 3 According to Postoperative Delirium Status
Number of Participants With Postoperative Delirium Assessed by the Confusion Assessment Method
title: Perioperative Biomarkers and Postoperative Delirium in Older Adults Undergoing Abdominal Cancer Surgery

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate whether the timing of intravenous ondansetron administration affects cerebral oxygenation and hemodynamic stability in older adults undergoing endoscopic urologic surgery under spinal anesthesia.

Participants aged 65 years or older will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: ondansetron administered before spinal anesthesia, ondansetron administered after spinal anesthesia, or placebo. Ondansetron will be administered intravenously at a dose of 8 mg.

Cerebral oxygenation will be assessed using bilateral frontal near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS). Regional cerebral oxygen saturation (rSO₂) will be recorded before spinal anesthesia and at 5-minute intervals during the first 60 minutes after spinal anesthesia.

The study will also evaluate blood pressure, heart rate, vasopressor requirements, bradycardia, postoperative nausea and vomiting, post-spinal headache, and postoperative delirium.

The aim is to determine whether the timing of ondansetron administration influences cerebral oxygenation and hemodynamic stability after spinal anesthesia.
primary_outcomes: Bilateral Frontal Regional Cerebral Oxygen Saturation (rSO₂)
title: Effects of Ondansetron Timing During Spinal Anesthesia for Urologic Surgery

brief_summary:
This clinical trial has two parts. In Part A, the goal is to learn about the safety and tolerability of COR-2003 when it is given alone. In Part B, the goal is to learn about the safety and tolerability of COR-2003 and COR-1004 when given together.

The main questions it aims to answer in Part A are:

* How well is COR-2003 absorbed in the blood?
* Do any medical problems develop in participants taking COR-2003?
* How well do participants tolerate COR-2003 compared to a placebo (a look-alike injection that contains no drug)?

The main questions it aims to answer in Part B are:

* How well are COR-1004 + COR-2003 absorbed in the blood when dosed at the same time?
* Do any medical problems develop in participants taking COR-1004 + COR-2003?
* How well do participants tolerate COR-1004 + COR-2003 compared to placebo + placebo (two look-alike injections that contains no drug)?

Participants will:

* Receive one or two subcutaneous injection(s) of COR-2003 or placebo (Part A) or receive two subcutaneous injections - one injection of COR-2003 and one injection of COR-1004 or two placebo injections (Part B).
* Visit the clinic for checkups and tests before the trial starts, complete a 3-night in-patient stay, followed by 14 follow up visits (monthly) until the trial ends (approximately 13 months).
conditions: Otherwise Healthy Individuals With Systolic Blood Pressure (SBP) From 110 to 139 mmHg and Low-density Lipoprotein Cholesterol (LDL-C) ≥ 100 mg/dL
primary_outcomes: Part A: Number and severity of adverse events and number of participants with adverse events to day 90 and until completion of the study
Part B: Number and severity of adverse events and number of participants with adverse events to day 90 and until completion of the study
title: A Study to Evaluate COR-2003 as Monotherapy and Co-Administered With COR-1004 in Adult Volunteers

brief_summary:
Older adults with chewing or swallowing difficulties may require texture-modified diets to reduce the risk of choking and aspiration. However, conventional texture-modified meals may be less visually appealing and may have lower energy and protein content because of the liquid added during pureeing. These factors may reduce food intake and increase the risk of poor nutrition.

This study will evaluate whether visually appealing, texture-modified soft meals prepared from familiar Asian foods can improve food and nutrient intake among older adults with chewing or swallowing difficulties. Up to 35 residents aged 60 years and above will be recruited from a nursing home in Singapore. Eligible participants must have reported chewing and/or swallowing difficulties and must have been consuming a texture-modified diet for at least six months.

The study will be conducted over two weeks. During the first week, participants will receive the nursing home's existing texture-modified menu. During the second week, they will receive soft versions of the same menu items. The soft meals will be prepared using an enzyme gellant and moulded to resemble the appearance of the original foods. The texture of the soft meals will be verified by the nursing home's speech therapist as safe and appropriate for each participant before the meals are served.

Food intake will be assessed at breakfast, lunch and dinner over seven days in each study week. Individual food items will be weighed before and after each meal to determine the amount consumed. Photographs of the food will also be taken before and after consumption to support assessment of intake. The amount of food consumed will be used to estimate participants' energy and nutrient intake.

The primary aim is to compare food intake during the soft-meal week with food intake during the existing-menu week. The study will provide preliminary evidence on whether familiar, visually appealing texture-modified soft meals can improve oral intake among nursing home residents with chewing or swallowing difficulties. The findings may inform future food-service practices for older adults who require texture-modified diets.
primary_outcomes: Change in Mean Daily Food Intake
title: Softer Meals That Impact the Life of the Elderly (SMILE) - Food Intake Study

brief_summary:
The aim of this clinical trial is to learn how whole-body vibration training and aerobic exercise training affect menstrual pain, symptom severity, and quality of life in young adult women with primary dysmenorrhea. Primary dysmenorrhea is menstrual pain that occurs without an underlying medical condition. It can interfere with daily activities and quality of life. Exercise may help manage menstrual pain, but more information is needed about the effects of different exercise approaches.

This study will examine the effects of whole-body vibration training and aerobic exercise training in young adult women with primary dysmenorrhea. Researchers will assess menstrual pain, the severity of menstrual symptoms, and quality of life. The findings may help inform exercise-based approaches to managing primary dysmenorrhea.
lead_sponsor: Gaziantep Islam Science and Technology University
title: Whole-Body Vibration and Aerobic Exercise for Primary Dysmenorrhea in Young Adult Women

brief_summary: This clinical trial is a Phase 2/3 study that will determine the recommended dose and dose regimen of AG-236 and evaluate the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics of AG-236 in polycythemia vera (PV) by testing how well AG-236 works compared to placebo to increase the number of subjects with no phlebotomy and absence of phlebotomy eligibility over a 13-week period. In addition, the long-term effect of AG-236 on efficacy and safety will be explored in an open-label extension portion.
primary_outcomes: Phase 2 and Phase 3: Percentage of Subjects With No Phlebotomy and Absence of Phlebotomy Eligibility
title: A Study to Investigate AG-236 in Subjects ≥18 Years of Age With Polycythemia Vera

brief_summary:
This prospective study compares two approaches to obtaining mature oocytes for fertility treatment within the same participant. Immature oocytes are first retrieved from the right ovary and matured in the laboratory using a two-step biphasic capacitation in vitro maturation method (CAPA-IVM). Beginning on Day 5 of the same menstrual cycle, the left ovary undergoes minimal controlled ovarian stimulation followed by routine oocyte retrieval and IVF/ICSI.

The primary objective is to evaluate the maturation of CAPA-IVM oocytes to the metaphase II (MII) stage and compare reproductive laboratory outcomes between the CAPA-IVM and minimal-stimulation OS-IVF approaches. Secondary outcomes include fertilization, embryo development, blastocyst formation, embryo quality, pregnancy and live birth outcomes, and safety.
primary_outcomes: Maturation Rate to Metaphase II (MII) Following CAPA-IVM
title: Intra-ovarian CAPA-IVM vs Standard IVM

brief_summary: This prospective, single-center interventional imaging study aims to evaluate the diagnostic performance of Photon Counting Computed Tomography (PCCT) combined with artificial intelligence-based Quantitative Coronary CT (AI-QCT) analysis in patients with suspected or known coronary artery disease (CAD).

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, perceived safety, and adherence outcomes of FIRST BITES (Food Introduction for Risk Reduction, Support Tolerance: Behavioral Intervention for Toddler Eating Success), a supervised, community-based early peanut introduction model, in caregiver-infant dyads.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can eligible caregiver-infant dyads be successfully recruited to and retained in community-based peanut introduction events, and do caregivers find the feeding event, educational materials, and intervention approach acceptable?
* Does education plus structured behavioral reinforcement improve adherence to peanut feeding recommendations, caregiver self-efficacy, and caregiver anxiety related to early peanut introduction compared with education alone?

Researchers will compare education alone with education plus behavioral reinforcement to determine whether behavioral reinforcement supports continued peanut feeding and improves caregiver confidence following peanut introduction.

Participants will:

* Attend a supervised community-based peanut introduction event.
* Receive education about early peanut introduction.
* Be randomized to receive either education alone or education plus behavioral reinforcement following the feeding event.
* Complete surveys regarding peanut feeding practices, caregiver self-efficacy, anxiety related to peanut introduction, and perceptions of feasibility, acceptability, and safety.
* Participate in follow-up assessments during the 6-week intervention period and at 3 months after enrollment.
* Some participants may be invited to complete qualitative interviews regarding barriers and facilitators to early peanut introduction.
lead_sponsor: University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center
primary_outcomes: Recruitment, Attendance, Retention, Assessment Completion, and Engagement Rates and Feasibility of Intervention Measure (FIM) Scores
Acceptability of Community Feeding Events and Behavioral Reinforcement Strategy Measured by Acceptability of Intervention Measure (AIM) Scores and Qualitative Interview Findings
Caregiver-Reported Comfort, Staff-Observed Safety Events, Adverse Events, Emergency Medical Interventions, and Safety Concerns During Supervised Peanut Introduction
Caregiver-Reported Peanut Offering, Peanut Ingestion, Feeding Frequency, and Peanut Protein Consumption
title: Food Introduction for Risk Reduction, Support Tolerance: Behavioral Intervention for Toddler Eating Success

brief_summary:
Chronic migraine is a disabling neurological disorder characterized by frequent headache attacks and significant impairment of quality of life. Low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFUS) is a non-invasive neuromodulation technique that can precisely target deep brain regions. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of LIFUS targeting the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) for preventive treatment of chronic migraine in adults.

This is a randomized, single-blind, sham-controlled clinical trial. Eligible participants with chronic migraine will be randomly assigned to receive either active LIFUS stimulation targeting the left DLPFC or sham stimulation. Participants will receive 10 stimulation sessions over 2 weeks and will be followed for 3 months after intervention.

The primary outcome is the change in monthly migraine days from baseline to 1 month after intervention. Secondary and exploratory outcomes include headache-related disability, quality of life, psychological assessments, electrophysiological measurements, neuroimaging changes, and safety outcomes.
title: Low-Intensity Focused Ultrasound Targeting the Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex for Preventive Treatment of Chronic Migraine

brief_summary:
This cross-sectional observational study aims to characterize acquired visual impairment in adults with acquired brain injury and to examine the relationship between objectively identified visual impairment and self-reported functional visual performance.

A total of 108 adults with acquired brain injury, including stroke, traumatic brain injury, and brain tumor, will undergo a standardized visual assessment. Objective visual function will be evaluated across five predefined domains: visual acuity, contrast sensitivity, visual field, oculomotor function, and visual attention/scanning. Self-reported functional visual performance will be assessed using the Revised Self-Report Assessment of Functional Visual Performance (R-SRAFVP).

The study will determine the proportion of participants with objectively identified visual impairment and examine the association between the R-SRAFVP score and the number of objectively impaired visual domains. The distribution of impairment across the individual visual domains will also be described.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants with objectively identified visual impairment
Association between R-SRAFVP score and number of objectively impaired visual domains
title: Visual Impairment and Functional Visual Performance Following Acquired Brain Injury: A Cross-Sectional Study

brief_summary:
Retained foreign objects, such as surgical sponges, needles, or instruments, are rare but potentially serious complications of surgery. When there is concern that an object may have been left behind, an intraoperative radiograph may be obtained while the patient is still in the operating room. These radiographs can be difficult to interpret because of overlapping surgical equipment, patient positioning, and the need for rapid interpretation.

This prospective observational study evaluates an artificial intelligence (AI) system designed to detect retained foreign objects on intraoperative radiographs. Eligible radiographs obtained during routine clinical care will be automatically processed by the AI system in real time for approximately one year. The AI results will not be shown to radiologists, surgeons, or other members of the clinical care team and will not affect patient care.

The study will evaluate how accurately the AI system detects retained foreign objects and how reliably and quickly the system operates in a real-world clinical environment.
primary_outcomes: Sensitivity of the AI System for Retained Foreign Object Detection
title: Prospective Silent Evaluation of AI for Retained Foreign Object Detection

brief_summary: This is an interventional clinical study. A total of 90 subjects aged 18 to 40 years are planned to be recruited. The subjects have low back pain that affects daily work and life, resulting in reduced exercise tolerance or aggravated pain after exercise, while retaining basic living ability and being capable of performing partial activities; their VAS scores range from 4 to 6. At baseline, the duration of subjects' low back pain and disability index will be recorded, along with muscle stiffness and electroencephalogram findings. Afterwards, electronic moxibustion treatment will be administered for 4 weeks. Subjects will be randomly divided into a treatment group and a control group with equal numbers of participants. The treatment group will use a Wenyang instrument with a rated frequency of 50 Hz, with the temperature set between 40℃ and 60℃ based on subjects' comfort level. Each treatment session lasts 30 to 60 minutes, 5 times per week for 4 weeks. The Wenyang instrument is used by subjects at home, with researchers providing remote guidance and supervision via voice or video. Subjects will check in and upload records after each use of electronic moxibustion, which will be documented by researchers. If subjects suffer from unbearable low back pain during the study, they may take oral ibuprofen or celecoxib for pain relief. The dosage and administration time will be recorded, and check-in and upload will be completed after each dose of analgesics for researchers' documentation. Subjects in the control group will take oral ibuprofen or celecoxib for pain relief as needed (i.e., when they feel pain). The dosage and administration time will be recorded with check-in and upload. After 4 weeks of intervention, the two groups will be compared in terms of the number of days of analgesic use or total consumed dosage, as well as changes in VAS scores, disability index, muscle stiffness and electroencephalogram findings.
title: Study on the Effect of Electronic Moxibustion on Non-Specific Low Back Pain in Young Adults

brief_summary:
B. Introduction Tennis elbow, medically termed lateral epicondylitis (LE), is a prevalent musculoskeletal disorder characterized by pain and tenderness over the lateral epicondyle of the humerus. Excessive mechanical stress on the elbow tendons, often caused by repetitive movements or manual labor, contributes to microtrauma and cumulative strain of the forearm and elbow musculature. Clinically, the site of maximal tenderness is situated just anterior and distal to the lateral epicondyle itself. Moreover, studies have demonstrated that pain intensity and grip strength are closely associated with manual test outcomes in chronic tennis elbow, further supporting the functional relevance of these diagnostic measures. Although historically associated with racquet sports, contemporary evidence indicates that the condition is more frequently linked to occupational and daily activities such as typing, carpentry, and healthcare work.Epidemiological studies estimate an annual prevalence of approximately 1.3% and an incidence of 3.4 per 1,000 individuals, making it one of the most common causes of elbow pain in adults aged 30-60 years.

The disorder exerts a considerable impact on modern life. Participants often experience reduced grip strength and functional limitations that interfere with essential tasks such as lifting, writing, or using tools. This functional impairment contributes to work productivity loss and increased healthcare utilization, resulting in substantial economic burden. Moreover, lifestyle factors such as smoking and repetitive manual work has been shown to negatively influence prognosis, with a subset of participants requiring surgical intervention after six months of unsuccessful conservative treatment. Collectively, these findings underscore that tennis elbow is not merely a sports-related injury but a significant occupational health issue, affecting individual well-being and societal efficiency in today's workforce.

A pilot randomize controlled cross-over trial of TCMO (Ng's prescription) in 2024 has significant efficacy on LE and can effectively improve the pain symptoms of participants (95%CI: -22.4 to -5.28, p: 0.0032). Modern drug treatments for tennis elbow mainly focus on reducing pain and inflammation. While this can provide short-term relief and help participants tolerate daily activities or rehabilitation, it often does not address the underlying tendon degeneration and impaired healing.

C. Trial Objective

1. Primary objective:

   To evaluate the efficacy of TCMO (Ng's prescription) in reducing pain intensity of LE through randomized controlled trial (RCT).
2. Secondary objective:

To evaluate safety of TCMO (Ng's prescription) of LE through randomized controlled trial (RCT). To assess functional improvement of TCMO (Ng's prescription) (PRTEE). Randomization and allocation concealment To minimize research bias, 48 participants will be assigned to two treatment groups and a control group in a 1:1 ratio. Block randomization via Sealed Envelope tool, with gender as the stratification criterion. Sealed opaque envelopes and password-protected file. RA generates sequence; Research Assistant II (RAII) blinded. To further minimize potential bias, evaluators and data analysts involved in the study will be blinded to treatment assignments. RAII will manage and analyze collected data. The PI will assess participant outcomes and oversee the entire study process. Group A: receive Topical Chinese Medicine Ointment (TCMO)（Ng's prescription）and eccentric exercise Group B: receive eccentric exercise only
title: Effectiveness of Topical Chinese Medicine Ointment Therapy (TCMO) (Ng's Prescription) Eccentric Exercise for Tennis Elbow as Control: a Randomized Controlled Trial.

brief_summary:
Roughly one patient in five never reaches the expected weight loss after MBS, and long-term regain after SG is well documented. These patients are identifiable at the 12-month visit. Today they are watched, coached, and treated only when failure is established.

Whether the drug works in this group is no longer the question. BARI-STEP, published this year, randomized 70 patients with less than 20% weight loss after gastric bypass (including one-anastomosis) or sleeve gastrectomy, a mean of seven years after surgery, to semaglutide 2.4 mg or placebo: 18.0% loss versus 0.4% gain at 68 weeks, an adjusted difference of 19.1 percentage points. Its population was mixed, 55.7% with recurrent weight gain and 44.3% with suboptimal initial response, and its exploratory comparison found no difference in drug response between the two presentations. BARI-OPTIMISE showed the same direction with liraglutide, as did a randomized trial after gastric banding. Efficacy is settled.

Timing is not. BARI-STEP recruited patients a mean of seven years past surgery, after failure had hardened. No trial has tested treating at first recognition, the 12-month visit, against the current standard of structured waiting. The field's own reviews name timing and duration as the open questions. The 2024 IFSO international consensus reached 100% agreement that medication after MBS should generally be withheld until the weight plateau, and 100% agreement that adding it for a suboptimal response can then improve outcomes. That is exactly our immediate arm: treat at the plateau, at first recognition. The triggered arm is what clinics actually do: wait for established failure. Both positions rest on expert agreement, not on a trial. This is the randomized test of the consensus pathway. A registered open-label pilot starts tirzepatide at 12 or 18 months but is small, unblinded, and not a strategy comparison.

The 2026 consensus draws the line for us, and this protocol respects it. The Delphi panel defined surgical nonresponse as less than 10% TWL at 12 months, defined recurrent weight gain as regain of more than 25% of lost weight from nadir, and treated a 10% swing in %EWL from nadir as normal physiologic fluctuation. It gave no 12-month label at all to the patient with 10 to 19.9% TWL, and the IFSO Delphi consensus expects the weight nadir up to 2 years after surgery (Obes Surg 2023). So a patient at 14% TWL at one year may still be on the way down, and calling that failure would be wrong. The protocol therefore splits eligibility into two tiers. Below 10% TWL at 12 months: consensus-defined nonresponse, randomized at once, waiting adds nothing. 10 to below 20% TWL: randomized only after a documented plateau, defined in Section 4, with a hard cap at month 18 so waiting cannot drift into neglect. Randomization is stratified by tier, and results are reported by tier.
lead_sponsor: General Committee of Teaching Hospitals and Institutes, Egypt
title: Immediate Versus Criterion-triggered Semaglutide for Suboptimal Clinical Response One Year After Primary Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery

brief_summary:
Stiff-knee gait (SKG) is a frequent gait abnormality in people with post-stroke hemiparesis and is characterized by insufficient knee flexion during the swing phase of walking. One potential mechanism is inappropriate activation of one or more heads of the quadriceps during pre-swing and early swing.

This observational study will compare quadriceps electromyographic activity and gait kinematics between adults with chronic post-stroke hemiparesis with SKG and healthy adult controls.

The study will include 30 participants with post-stroke SKG and 24 healthy controls. Quantitative gait analysis will be performed using three-dimensional motion analysis together with electromyography (EMG). Ultrasound-guided fine-wire electrodes will record the activity of all four heads of the quadriceps: rectus femoris, vastus intermedius, vastus medialis, and vastus lateralis.

Healthy controls will be assessed while walking at a slow speed selected to provide a reference condition that is comparable with the walking speeds typically observed in participants with post-stroke hemiparesis.

The primary outcome is the difference in fine-wire EMG activation patterns of the four quadriceps heads between participants with post-stroke SKG and healthy controls, with particular attention to pre-swing and early swing.

Secondary outcomes will assess differences in gait kinematics between groups, including peak knee flexion during the swing phase and knee flexion-extension patterns throughout the gait cycle.

The study aims to improve understanding of the muscular mechanisms underlying post-stroke SKG and to establish relevant fine-wire EMG reference patterns for all four quadriceps heads in healthy individuals walking at a speed comparable with patients with hemiparesis.
primary_outcomes: On-Off Quadriceps Electromyographic Activity During the Gait Cycle
title: Quadriceps Muscle Activity and Gait Kinematics in Patients With Post-Stroke Stiff-Knee Gait Compared With Healthy Controls

brief_summary: Early gastric cancer (EGC) is traditionally treated with either endoscopic resection or standard laparoscopic gastrectomy with formal lymph node dissection. However, endoscopic resection cannot evaluate or treat regional lymph node metastasis, whereas standard surgery significantly impairs postoperative gastric physiological function and patient quality of life (QoL). The LENS trial is a prospective, single-arm clinical study designed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and long-term efficacy of Laparoscopic and Endoscopic Cooperative Surgery (LECS) combined with Laparoscopic Sentinel Node Navigation Surgery (LSNNS) using Indocyanine Green (ICG) fluorescence tracing for patients with cT1N0M0 early gastric cancer. In this trial, eligible patients will undergo intraoperative sentinel lymph node (SN) biopsy guided by ICG. Patients with negative SN status will receive stomach-preserving surgery (primarily Non-exposed Endoscopic Wall-inversion Surgery, NEWS), while those with positive SN status will convert to standard laparoscopic gastrectomy. The primary goal is to confirm whether this combined procedure provides long-term oncological safety comparable to standard radical gastrectomy, while significantly improving postoperative gastric function, nutritional status, and quality of life.
title: LECS Combined With LSNNS for Early Gastric Cancer (LENS Trial)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether the Triojection® System is safe and effective for treating symptomatic lumbar radiculopathy (leg pain caused by nerve irritation or compression) resulting from a contained herniated lumbar disc. The study will enroll adults 18 to 75 years of age with a single-level contained lumbar disc herniation who continue to have symptoms despite at least 6 weeks of non-surgical treatment and a previous lumbar spine injection.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does treatment with the Triojection® System improve leg pain and overall clinical outcomes compared with Selective Nerve Root Block (SNRB) alone?
* Is treatment with the Triojection® System safe, as measured by the absence of device- or procedure-related serious adverse events and persistent neurological deficits?

Researchers will compare participants who receive Triojection® followed by SNRB with participants who receive SNRB alone to determine whether the investigational treatment provides improved clinical outcomes.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to receive either Triojection® plus SNRB or SNRB alone.
* Complete questionnaires about leg pain, back pain, disability, quality of life, sleep, anxiety, depression, and overall improvement.
* Undergo physical and neurological examinations during study follow-up visits.
* Have MRI scans performed at selected study visits to evaluate changes in the treated disc.
* Attend follow-up visits at 1, 3, 6, 12, 18, and 24 months after treatment.

Up to 300 participants will be enrolled at up to 30 investigational sites in the United States and Canada and followed for approximately 24 months after treatment.

brief_summary:
The NHS provides specialist consultant services to primary care clinicians for decision-making support and planning patient care. The consultation takes place as an 'in-person' event at a secondary care centre where the consultant services are based (Teaching or district hospitals). This model is used ubiquitously for oral health care and other medical services. There is a drive to deliver this service in a more patient-centred, cost-effective, efficient manner, addressing the NHS plan for a 30% reduction of OP visits (NHS Long Term Plan v1.2, August 2019) and in an environmentally sustainable manner by reducing unnecessary patient travel - 31% of NHS-Dentistry carbon foot print. Remote Clinical Consultations (RCC) have the potential to offer this service by linking both the primary care clinician and the patient (co-located in the dental practice) to a remote specialist consultant, using super-fast internet connectivity.

This enables all the participants (Patient, GDP and consultant) to hold a live 3-way patient-centred discussion about the patient's care needs. Our research team has recently completed a comprehensive service evaluation that identifies RCC as being technically feasible with a high level of patient acceptability. A further PoC feasibility clinical study to test the RCC concept in a dental primary care setting will be conducted. For this, strong collaborative alliance with AMRC (Digital Design \& Prototyping Group), the Department of Physics and IT Services- STHNHS and a local primary care dental practice consortium (Dental Partners PLC) have been established. Following on from this, a multi-centre randomised clinical trial in a wider range of settings to determine the cost-effectiveness of this clinical intervention will be undertaken
lead_sponsor: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
primary_outcomes: Establish the viability and efficiency of a remote specialist consultation process as a means delivering a patient-centred treatment strategy, in a manner that is not inferior to an 'in-person' event.
title: Remote Clinical Consultations in Restorative Dentistry for Primary Care

brief_summary:
The primary aim of this study is to evaluate HMGB1 levels in cases of intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR).

The secondary aim is to determine whether the cerebroplacental ratio interacts with these levels.

IUGR occurs when the fetus fails to reach its expected uterine growth potential due to fetal, maternal, and/or placental factors. IUGR occurs in approximately 10% of pregnancies worldwide. IUGR is associated with high perinatal morbidity and mortality rates.

High motility group box 1 (HMGB1) is the most abundant member of the high motility group (HMG) protein family and is expressed in almost all human cells. HMGB1 is predominantly found in the nucleus and can also shuttle actively and passively between the nucleus and cytoplasm. During cell apoptosis and necrosis, HMGB1 is released from dying cells into the extracellular space.

In high-risk pregnancies, particularly preeclampsia, HMGB1 levels are known to be elevated in the maternal circulation. A study investigating the possible link between sterile inflammation mediated by HMGB1 and the angiogenic imbalance observed in preeclampsia showed that high HMGB1 expression and its release from hypoxic trophoblasts play a critical role and contribute to angiogenic imbalance in preeclampsia.
title: HMGB1 Levels at Fetal Growth Restriction
